data.name: Leonardo Da Vinci in Florence - Private Tour
data.description: City Florence Tours invites you to discover one of the most fascinating minds of the Renaissance, with a guided tour that will take you to admire the most beloved Florentine places of the master Leonardo Da Vinci, showing you unusual details about his person and how the city looked of Florence at the end of the 15th century. You will start at the Bargello Museum, visit Palazzo Gondi, arrive in the square of the Uffizi Gallery and continue your visit, walk along Piazza Della Signoria where you can admire the Palazzo Vecchio and the Salone dei 500, which is located at interior of the building. Turning your back on the building, you will admire the Loggia dei Lanzi, then walk past the Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore, to admire the Dome. The last leg of our visit will be the Leonardo Da Vinci Museum in Florence, we will enter inside to visit this small museum entirely dedicated to the master, containing replicas and drawings of the main machines made by the genius.

data.name: Florence: Food Market Tour and Guided Pasta Cooking Class
data.description: Experience the flavors of Florence like a local during this hands-on pasta-making class and market tour. Your expert guide will share insights into the best local ingredients as you explore a bustling food market, before you learn how to make traditional homemade ravioli, tagliatelle, or tagliolini with a professional chef. Your experience culminates in a delicious 3-course meal, including an appetizer, dessert, and two paired wines.

data.name: Palazzo Pitti - Priority Ticket
data.description:
Come and visit the last Medici residence in Florence. The museum takes place through the daily life of the Medici Grand Dukes family, from Cosimo I to the last descendants (early 18th century), Ferdinando, Gian Gastone and lastly Anna Maria Luisa also known as the Palatine Electress to whom it is dedicated the museum. The successors of the Medici, the Habsburg Lorraine, up to the first King of Italy with adjoining Royal apartments.

In addition to the civic and political function of the rooms, the museum also preserves a private collection of Florentine paintings, ancient statues, furniture and mosaics of great beauty and historical importance. Not to mention the frescoes that decorate the ceilings and walls.

By purchasing this type of ticket, you will have the opportunity to additionally purchase the ticket for the Boboli Gardens.

data.name: Palazzo Pitti & Boboli Gardens Pass
data.shortDescription: Enjoy Florence's art, history and lush gardens with this convenient pass
data.description:
The Pitti Palace & Boboli Gardens Pass will take your Florence experience to the next level!

Among the attractions at Florence's Renaissance-era Boboli Gardens are the Egyptian obelisk and the Fountain of Neptune. Tickets for the Porcelain Museum and Bardini Gardens are also included. 

Next, explore the magnificent Palazzo Pitti. Take in the luxurious rooms of the grand royal palace and see masterpieces by Raphael, Titian, and Rubens in the Palatine Gallery. 

Using the two included audio guides, you can easily self-guide your adventures through Florence. Explore the city and Palazzo Pitti independently using the interactive map and audio commentary and find out local insider tips on where to eat and take the best photos!

data.name: Chianti: Guided Winery Tour + Wines & Cheeses Tasting
data.shortDescription: Taste traditional wines at a family-owned Chianti winery paired with cheese
data.description:
Prepare for a wine-tasting tour at a family-owned vineyard. Visit the cellars in the winery and learn about the history and wine-making process while you see the machinery and barrels up close.

Taste 4 different wines, i.e., two IGT Toscana wines, one Chianti Classico, and one Chianti Classico RISERVA, paired with local cheeses. Also, the hosts will guide you through each tasting, explaining the flavors.

Enjoy Tuscan crackers and local cheeses, and take a stroll through the vineyards if you like. Extra food, wines, liquors, and spirits are available for an additional fee.

data.name: Entrance Ticket To Basilica of Santa Croce
data.shortDescription:
The Franciscan Church of Santa Croce is one of the most beloved places in Florence because of the richness of its artistic heritage, the civic value of its funerary monuments and, above all, because this great structure symbolizes the relationship between Christian faith, art and culture in Florence and in Italy.

Its construction began in 1295, at the expense of the people and the Florentine Republic, and since then its history has been deeply intertwined with the history of the city itself.

In fact, over the centuries, spiritual, artistic and civic testimonies trace its complex identity, until in the 19th century it became a monument symbolizing the unity of the new nation. In the complex of church, cloister and museum you can admire famous works of art, fruit of Christian ingenuity and devotion of artists such as Arnolfo di Cambio, Cimabue, Giotto, Filippo Brunelleschi, Donatello, Giorgio Vasari, Lorenzo Ghiberti, Orcagna, Taddeo and Agnolo Gaddi, Della Robbia, Giovanni da Milano, Bronzino, Domenico Veneziano, Maso di Banco, Canova and others.

Santa Croce has been called "the pantheon of Italian glory" because it contains the tombs of such illustrious figures as Michelangelo Buonarroti, Galileo Galilei, Niccolò Machiavelli, Gioachino Rossini, Lorenzo Ghiberti, Vittorio Alfieri and Ugo Foscolo.

data.name: Museo Ferragamo Entrance Tickets
data.shortDescription:
The eleventh of fourteen children, Salvatore Ferragamo was born in 1898 in Bonito, a small village 100 kilometres from Naples. Even as a child, Salvatore showed a great passion for shoes: at the age of 11 he was apprenticed to a shoemaker in Naples and at 13 he opened his own shop in Bonito. When he was 16, he travelled to America to join one of his brothers who was working for a large shoe factory in Boston. Salvatore was fascinated by the modern machinery and production processes but he also saw how they could limit product quality. In the early Twenties he moved to Santa Barbara, California, where he opened a shoemaking and repair shop. California was an exciting place to be at that time with the new film industry booming. Salvatore began designing and making shoes for the movies. Meanwhile, in his ongoing search for shoes with the perfect fit, he studied human anatomy, chemical engineering and mathematics at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles.

When the movie industry moved to Hollywood, Salvatore Ferragamo went with it. In 1923 he opened the ‘Hollywood Boot Shop’, which marked the start of his career as ‘shoemaker to the stars’, as he was defined by the local press. In 1927 Ferragamo decided to return to his native Italy and chose to settle in Florence, a city known for its many skilled craftsmen. From his Florentine workshop – in which he adapted the assembly line system to his workers’ highly specialised and strictly manual work – Salvatore launched a constant flow of exports to the United States.

Then came the great crisis of 1929, which abruptly brought business with the US market to a standstill and forced the company to close. However, Ferragamo did not lose heart. Instead, he turned his focus to the domestic market. Within a few years, his business was performing so well that in 1936 he rented two workshops and a shop in Palazzo Spini Feroni, via Tornabuoni, Florence. Despite the economic sanctions against Mussolini’s Italy, it was during this time that Ferragamo turned out some of his most popular and widely-imitated creations, like his strong, yet light cork ‘wedges’. In 1938 these successful creations enabled him to pay the first instalment for the purchase of all of Palazzo Spini Feroni, which has been the company’s headquarters ever since. In 1940 he married the young daughter of the local doctor in Bonito, Wanda Miletti, who joined him in Florence and would bear him six children: three sons (Ferruccio, Leonardo and Massimo) and three daughters (Fiamma, Giovanna and Fulvia).

After the war, Salvatore Ferragamo’s shoes came to be known around the world as a symbol of Italy’s return to life, design and production. The years that followed saw many memorable inventions: the stiletto heels with metal reinforcement made famous by Marilyn Monroe, the gold sandals and the invisible sandals with nylon thread uppers (for which Ferragamo won the prestigious ‘Neiman Marcus Award’ in 1947, the fashion world’s equivalent of the Oscar, marking the first time it was bestowed on a shoe designer).

When the movie industry moved to Hollywood, Salvatore Ferragamo went with it. In 1927 Ferragamo decided to return to his native Italy and chose to settle in Florence, a city known for its many skilled craftsmen. From his Florentine workshop – in which he adapted the assembly line system to his workers’ highly specialised and strictly manual work – Salvatore launched a constant flow of exports to the United States.

Then came the great crisis of 1929, which abruptly brought business with the US market to a standstill and forced the company to close. However, Ferragamo did not lose heart. Instead, he turned his focus to the domestic market. Within a few years, his business was performing so well that in 1936 he rented two workshops and a shop in Palazzo Spini Feroni, via Tornabuoni, Florence. Despite the economic sanctions against Mussolini’s Italy, it was during this time that Ferragamo turned out some of his most popular and widely-imitated creations, like his strong, yet light cork ‘wedges’. In 1938 these successful creations enabled him to pay the first instalment for the purchase of all of Palazzo Spini Feroni, which has been the company’s headquarters ever since. In 1940 he married the young daughter of the local doctor in Bonito, Wanda Miletti, who joined him in Florence and would bear him six children: three sons (Ferruccio, Leonardo and Massimo) and three daughters (Fiamma, Giovanna and Fulvia).

After the war, Salvatore Ferragamo’s shoes came to be known around the world as a symbol of Italy’s return to life, design and production. The years that followed saw many memorable inventions: the stiletto heels with metal reinforcement made famous by Marilyn Monroe, the gold sandals and the invisible sandals with nylon thread uppers (for which Ferragamo won the prestigious ‘Neiman Marcus Award’ in 1947, the fashion world’s equivalent of the Oscar, marking the first time it was bestowed on a shoe designer).

data.name: Florence Duomo Tour with Giotto Pass
data.description: Explore the Opera del Duomo complex in Florence with a Giotto pass, and avoid the problem of long waits with priority access to the cathedral, crypt, museum, Giotto's Bell Tower, and baptistery. Learn about the fascinating history and architectural brilliance of Brunelleschi’s Dome and other Renaissance masterpieces from an expert guide. After the tour, admire every intricate detail of these iconic landmarks at your own pace.

data.name: Tuscan Countryside Full-Day Bike Tour from Florence
data.description: Experience the joy of cycling through Tuscany on this full-day bicycle tour from Florence. Travel by van to the heart of the famous Chianti wine region, where you’ll climb on a bike for a day of adventure. Visit one of the only remaining private Tuscan castles in the region, where you have the tour the grounds and learn how wine and olive oil are produced. A traditional Tuscan lunch with wine is included.

data.name: Florence tour with private shooting and photographer 2 hours
data.description:
Discover the most beautiful places in Florence with our professional photographer and our tour leader who will take a wonderful shooting in Piazza del Duomo, Piazza della Repubblica, Piazza della Signoria and Ponte Vecchio.

You will not be a passive spectator, but you will be the center of attention, free to enjoy the city without any cameras or various devices.

Once the tour is over the photographic material will be shared telematically already edited.

data.name: From Florence to Chianti: Tuscan Pasta Class for Couples
data.description:
Escape to the Tuscan countryside for a romantic pasta-making experience designed just for couples. Hosted at a charming family-run farm near Florence, this semi-private class (max 4 guests) offers the perfect blend of authenticity, intimacy, and stunning scenery.

Together, you’ll learn the art of fresh pasta preparation using traditional methods and seasonal ingredients from the farm’s garden. Set in a cozy farmhouse kitchen and guided by a passionate local host, this experience feels like stepping into a slower, more beautiful way of life.

After your hands-on workshop, savor your handmade pasta over a relaxed al fresco lunch, perfectly paired with local wine — surrounded by olive groves and rolling Tuscan hills.

Round-trip transportation from Florence is included, making it a seamless and unforgettable escape crafted with couples in mind.

data.name: Legacy of Michelangelo Walking Tour
data.description: Discover the works of Michelangelo and his impact on Florence with our two-hour walking tour. Witness iconic landmarks such as the Palazzo Vecchio, Uffizi Gallery, and the Bargello National Museum, where Michelangelo’s work and legacy are displayed. Hear intriguing stories about each object and their relation to Michelangelo, including the Basilica di Santo Spirito and the Basilica of Santa Croce, both of which hold important works by Michelangelo. Stop at the Casa Buonarroti, the birthplace of Michelangelo, and the Opera del Duomo Museum. End the tour in front of Basilica di San Lorenzo and the Accademia Gallery and enjoy storytelling on his renowned works including “David” and “The Prisoners”. Join us on this journey through Florence and Michelangelo’s heritage.

data.name: Florence Accademia Gallery & David Skip-the-line Small Group Tour
data.description: The Accademia Gallery is one of Florence’s most popular attractions, with the lines to match. Dodge the crowds and spend longer exploring the collection during this guided small-group tour, which includes skip-the-line admission tickets. In a group capped at 14 (headphones included), you’ll visit highlights like a rare Stradivari viola, priceless Renaissance paintings, and—the museum’s star attraction—Michelangelo’s *David*.

data.name: Best of Florence walking tour  - monolingual small group tour
data.description: The city of the Renaissance is literally dotted with ARCHITECTURAL WONDERS and WORKS OF ART, joining our tour you can admire with your own eyes the sites and monuments that have made Florence one of the most visited destinations in the world.The first stage of this enlightening guided promenade will be REPUBBLICA SQUARE, one of the most elegant squares in Florence, where the most refined cafés of the city are located. Follow your guide through the most characteristic streets and alleys until you reach the LOGGIA DEL MERCATO NUOVO, where you will discover how to win good luck caressing the nose of the famous PORCELLINO (wild boar) BRONZE STATUE.At a stone throw there is the suggestive PONTE VECCHIO, a true icon of the city, famous for hosting the most exclusive jewelry stores of Florence and for its unique structure, and also for being the only bridge of the city spared from the bombings during the Second World War.Follow your guide to the ACCADEMIA DEI GEORGOFILI and the UFFIZI SQUARE, and discover the beating heart of Florence, SIGNORIA SQUARE, a real open-air museum dominated by the imposing PALAZZO VECCHIO and the magnificent LOGGIA DEI LANZI, which houses wonderful original statues including the PERSEUS by Cellini and the RAT OF THE SABINE WOMEN by Giambologna.The journey to discover the wonders of Florence will culminate in SAN GIOVANNI SQUARE, home of the wonderful DUOMO and BRUNELLESCHI'S DOME as well as the Baptistery and Giotto's Bell Tower.

data.name: Dan Brown 'INFERNO' Florence Tour
data.shortDescription:
“The Palazzo Vecchio resembles a giant chess piece. With its robust quadrangular facade and rusticated square-cut battlements, the massive rooklike building is aptly situated, guarding the southeast corner of the Piazza della Signoria”.

This is what Dan Brown writes in his latest bestseller, Inferno, set in Florence, and mostly at the Palazzo Vecchio. Follow the steps of professor Robert Langdon and learn about the history of the palace as you move through the locations and scenes of the novel. The public rooms – as well as the most secret – become the settings for searches, pursuits, and coups de théâtre centered on a precise work of art.

“Here we are, finally… Marta Alvarez had expected to see Dante’s familiar dead face staring back at her, but instead, all she saw was the red satin interior of the cabinet and the peg on which the mask normally hung.”

data.name: GALILEO GALILEI MUSEUM  ENTRANCE TICKET  MUSEMENT
data.shortDescription:
The Institute and Museum for the History of Science greatly expanded in recent decades. The visibility of the museum soared thanks to its numerous activities and to the temporary exhibitions it organized, many of them highly successful on an international level. The museum has thus come to the forefront in the public eye, overshadowing the activities of research and documentation. The museum itself and its contents have been radically changed in recent years. And, thanks to the massive investment over the last twenty years in information and communication technology, the Institute has created digital archives of vital importance to research in the history of science.  .

It is only fitting that these changes prompted a new name: Museo Galileo. The subtitle, Istituto e Museo di Storia della Scienza (Institute and Museum for the History of Science), provides a link to its earlier history and shows that the activities of documentation and research have always been, are now, and will continue to be, the focus of highest attention.

Historical Notes

The Institute and Museum for the History of Science is heir to a tradition of five centuries of scientific collecting, which has its origins in the central importance assigned by the Medici and Lorraine families to scientists and scientific instruments.

The Medici: A Dynasty of Collectors

1562 - The Medici Wardrobe
The Medicean collection of scientific instruments was begun by Cosimo I (1519-1574), who housed it in the “Wardrobe” of the Palazzo Vecchio, known today as the "sala delle carte geografiche" (Map Room). The room was decorated between 1563 and 1581 by Egnazio Danti and Stefano Buonsignori, who painted the geography of the known world on the 57 doors of the wardrobe. Against the end wall was the planetary clock by Lorenzo della Volpaia. According to the original project, two large globes, one terrestrial, the other celestial, were to hang from the ceiling.

1600 - Mathematics Room
In 1600, Ferdinand I (1549-1609) transferred the collection to a small room in the Uffizi Gallery which became known as the "stanzino delle matematiche". Giulio Parigi depicted the instruments in the collection on the ceiling. Here and on the adjoining terrace (which once housed the great armillary sphere built by Antonio Santucci in 1593) the instruments bequeathed by Robert Dudley and those purchased in Germany by Mattias de\' Medici were displayed.

1657 - The Accademia del Cimento
With the foundation of the Accademia del Cimento (1657), inaugurated by Ferdinand II (1610-1670) and Leopold de\' Medici (1617-1675) for the purpose of conducting the experimental investigation of nature, the collection was enriched with new instruments designed mainly for thermometric, barometric, and pneumatic research. The Accademia was located in the Pitti Palace where all the instruments in the Medici collection were subsequently moved.

The Lorraine Collections

1775 - The Museum of Physics
In 1775 the instruments were moved from the Pitti Palace to the Royal Museum of Physics and Natural History in Palazzo Torrigiani on Via Romana, where the Specola Museum is located today. Grand Duke Peter Leopold Habsburg-Lorraine (1747-1792) appointed as director of the museum Abbot Felice Fontana, who built an observatory and upgraded the collection with new mathematics, physics, meteorology, an electricity instruments, many of which were constructed in the Museum workshops.

1829 - The Museum Workshops
After their decline during the Napoleonic occupation (1799-1814), the museum and its workshops were reorganized upon the return to power of the Lorraine Family. Under the direction of Vincenzo Antinori, outstanding astronomers and physicists such as Giovanni Battista Amici, constructor of microscopes, telescopes, micrometers, and spectroscopes, and Leopoldo Nobili, inventor of electromagnetic and galvanometric instruments and thermo-electric piles, contributed to the development of the Museum workshops.

1841 - The Tribune of Galileo
The Tribune was built in 1841 in the Museum of Physics, upon the initiative of Leopold II (1797-1870). The architect Giuseppe Martelli planned it to include a statue of Galileo, surrounded by frescoes and bas-reliefs illustrating the discoveries and the most important instruments of the great scientist: the geometric and military compass, an armed loadstone, two telescopes, and the objective lens of the telescope with which Galileo discovered the Jupiter satellites. The Renaissance instruments and those of the Accademia del Cimento were also displayed in the Tribune.

Since 1927

1927 - The Institute of the History of Science
After the Unification of Italy, the collections were dispersed among several university departments. In 1922, thanks to the promoters of the "Group for the Preservation of National Scientific Heritage," the collections were rescued from abandonment. In 1927, thanks to their commitment, the Istituto di Storia delle Scienze (The Institute of the History of Science) was founded, with the goal of "collecting, cataloging, and restoring" the scientific collections.

1929 - The National Exhibition
In 1929, the newborn Institute organized the First National Exhibition of the History of Science in Florence. Numerous Italian institutions participated in the show, which brought attention to the vast Italian scientific heritage, promoted its nationwide diffusion, and drew attention to the poor state of preservation. In 1930, following the show, the University of Florence opened the permanent exhibition of the Istituto di Storia della Scienza at Palazzo Castellani to the public. It included the Medici-Lorraine collection of instruments.

1966 - The Flood
After the damage caused by the bombings that destroyed the bridges of the Lungarno at the end of the Second World War (1944-45), another hard blow was dealt to the collection by the flood of 1966. The instruments that were stored in the basement and ground floor of the Museo were seriously damaged. Thanks to international solidarity and the efforts of Maria Luisa Righini Bonelli, then-director of the Museum, it was possible to quickly carry out recovery of the instruments, reopen the exhibition rooms to the public, and focus again on library collecting and research activities.

data.name: The best of Florence walking tour
data.description: Have you ever wondered why Florence was the birthplace of the Renaissance? This complete introductory tour is dedicated to those who want to know all the facts and secrets of two thousand years of Florentine history!Learn about the city's Roman origins, see the 15th-century palaces, Ponte Vecchio, the famous Uffizi courtyard, and the amazing Brunelleschi's Dome that overlooks the Baptistery's golden Gates of Paradise.Don't miss the chance to get close to this amazing city, understanding and appreciating the background and history. Nothing is better than discovering the city with an expert local guide.

data.name: Private Florence Artisans and Shopping tour
data.description: Enjoy the less beaten tracks of Florence with a tour through the arts of Florence. Florence arts craft is rich and dates back to centuries ago. This is the right tour to see some of the most hidden areas of Florence and discover its traditions, its people, its most authentic made in Italy products out of the usual touristy paths. Jewels and Goldsmith, Florentine mosaic. leather, shoes, paper and book binding are the workshops you will visit and where you will learn about these old traditional Florence handicrafts.

data.name: Cinque Terre Tour and Portovenere with Typical Lunch from Florence
data.description: Explore the breathtaking Ligurian coast on a tour of Cinque Terre, a small corner of paradise divided into five villages suspended on steep cliffs overlooking the sea; a unique landscape where vegetation and lush vineyards frame a spectacular scenery. Visit four of the five villages.You will spend an unforgettable day discovering one of the most impressive Ligurian landscapes. In this area, which has been declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO, earth and sea blend to create a unique landscape. The area consists of kilometres of rocky coasts with caves, beaches, hiking paths and breathtaking views. Meet our staff in Florence, where the tour will begin. You’ll first reach Manarola, a tiny urban jewel characterized by Genoese style ‘case-torri’. Then you will move to Vernazza, a village overlooked by the remains of a Medieval castle with a cylindrical tower, in which you can enjoy some free time. After that you will reach Monterosso, known as the ‘pearl of Cinque Terre’. This ancient fishing village with lovely beaches and lush vegetation covering the rocks that will certainly astonish you. First you’ll have a typical Ligurian lunch, where you’ll get the chance to taste the handmade pasta “trofie” with Pesto sauce, and other typical delicatessen, all accompanied by the kindness of the staff and relaxing music. After lunch you’ll also get the chance to take a swim as this is the biggest village with a perfect sandy beach and crystalline water. After that you’ll enjoy the village of Portovenere a small village plenty of several colored houses. Enjoy some free time before heading back to La Spezia where the train will be waiting for you. Enjoy a pleasant ride back to Florence where the tour will end.

data.name: Florence's Italian Opera Night with Dinner
data.description: Start your evening with a delicious Tuscan meal at a cozy trattoria before heading to an unforgettable performance of Italian opera in the Santa Monaca Church. Just a short stroll away, the medieval church’s ancient stone walls and rich acoustics create the perfect setting for timeless arias by Italy’s greatest composers. It’s a night of Florence’s finest, blending culinary tradition with musical heritage.

data.name: Private Day Trip from Florence to Pisa, Lucca and Vinci
data.description: On this full-day tour we'll first stop in Pisa, where you can see the impressive Piazza dei Miracoli as your driver/guide discusses the historic buildings around you. See the Baptistery, the Duomo and the city’s most iconic attraction, the UNESCO-listed Leaning Tower of Pisa.  From Pisa we'll drive to Vinci to discover the countryside where one of the most brilliant Renaissance personalities, Leonardo da Vinci, was born and lived. Visit his birthplace, a farmhouse in the town of Anchiano. After we will head to Lucca, by the time we get there it will be time for lunch, your driver will recommend you a local restaurant where you can enjoy an authentic Italian meal. After lunch we will go for a walking tour to admire the main attractions of the city, such as the Anfiteatro Square, the Guinigi Tower, San Martino Cathedral and a stroll along the picturesque streets of antique shops. Before we leave Lucca you will have some free time to enjoy a slice of Buccellato - Lucca’s traditional cake.

data.name: Florence Private Davanzati Palace Tour
data.description:
Make your own way to the Palazzo Davanzati to meet your guide for your private tour.

Learn about the history of the building, which was built in the late 1400s and purchased by the Davanzati family in 1578. Your guide shares details about the architecture, furniture styles, and the extensive collection of artifacts as you walk through the sumptuously decorated rooms. It now is known as the Museum of the Ancient Florentine House, and it provides a glimpse into the lifestyle of the aristocracy in Florence during the 14th and 15th centuries.

data.name: Florence Small-Group Gourmet Cooking Class with Dinner
data.description: Learn to cook like a Florentine during this small-group gourmet cooking lesson in Florence. Enjoy instruction from a multilingual professional chef who provides simple, clear guidance as you learn to prepare authentic savory and sweet dishes. Sip delicious Tuscan wine and feast on the meal you create inside a historic wine cellar in the heart of Florence.

data.name: Florence Uffizi Gallery Small-Group Tour
data.description: The vast collection at the Uffizi Gallery can be daunting even to passionate art enthusiasts. Cut the museum down to size with this small-group tour that focuses on the highlights to cover the collection in just hours. Zip past the line with fast-track admission and marvel at works by Botticelli, Michelangelo, Da Vinci, and other greats as you learn about their lives and masterpieces from your guide.

data.name: Florence Hills and Views Private Guided E-Bike Tour
data.description:
See Florence on this unique electric scooter excursion. Beginning in the center of the city, meet your guide for a brief safety overview to ensure you’re comfortable before hitting the streets.

With your local guide leading the way, head through the charming streets toward the historic city center. Travel from the lively Piazza della Repubblica to the Basilica of Santa Croce, pausing to admire its impressive white and green marble façade. Hear about the host of famous Italians buried here, such as Michelangelo and Galileo, before setting off to Piazza della Signoria.

Once there, discover why this square is described by many as the beating heart of the city. Look up to see the Palazzo Vecchio, once home to the powerful Medici family, as well as the collection of outdoor statues, including a replica of Michelangelo’s 'David.'

Continue to the Strozzi Palace and then to the architectural gem of Florence, the Duomo. See Brunelleschi’s famous dome up close, along with the Baptistery and Giotto’s Bell Tower.

Your tour will conclude at your original departure point.

data.name: Santo Stefano Auditorium: Three Tenors Concert
data.description: Ready for the goosebumps? See this tribute to The Three Tenors in one of Florence's best concert venues and you'll be getting the shivers. Hear Neapolitan classics like _O Sole Mio_, _Funiculì Funiculà_ and _Torna a Surriento_ performed by some of Italy's most impressive talent!

data.name: Medici Chapels: Skip The Line Ticket
data.shortDescription: Get up close to three Michelangelo masterpieces
data.description: The two Medici Chapels, in the Basilica of San Lorenzo, are an incredibly lavish mausoleum and a key site on the Florence Renaissance trail. After all, they not only contain three beautiful Michelangelo sculptures, they're also the final resting place for 49 members of the powerful Medici clan. Skip the lines and get into this spectacular Renaissance church.

data.name: Pasta class
data.description:
Step into a culinary time capsule in the heart of Florence! Our morning cooking class isn't just about making pasta—it's a thrilling journey back in time to the roots of Tuscan cuisine. Imagine crafting delicate pappardelle, pillowy gnocchi, and exquisite ravioli, all with your own hands, just like generations before us did.

"We will cook in an old tower house transformed into a modern kitchen." a haven where tradition meets innovation. Here, we shun modern machinery in favor of old-world techniques, infusing every dish with the authenticity and soul that define true home cooking.

And the magic doesn't stop there. As we craft each masterpiece, we'll elevate the experience with perfectly paired Chianti wines

Don't miss this opportunity to immerse yourself in the culinary heartbeat of Florence. Join us for a morning of discovery, creation, and indulgence that promises to ignite your passion for Italian cuisine. Book now and prepare to embark on a culinary adventure like no other!

data.name: Florence: Coffee, Chocolate, and Sweets Private Food Tour
data.description: Enjoy a Florence culinary tour like no other—and visit locally beloved bakeries, coffee shops and more, which many other visitors miss—on this private tasting tour. Make a variety of stops, from a traditional café where you’ll learn about the history of Italian coffee to gelaterias, chocolatiers, and other gourmet food businesses.

data.name: Florence and Chianti Driving Tour with Wine Tasting
data.description: Combine sightseeing in Florence with a wine-tasting excursion to a winery in the Chianti countryside with this private tour. Enjoy the ease of hotel pickup and take in the city’s sights with your driver before heading to Chianti. Stop at a Tuscan winery to visit the vineyard, barrel room, and other production areas, then relax over a tasting featuring five wines, pecorino cheese, extra-virgin olive oil, truffle-flavored olive oil, and balsamic vinegar.

data.name: Florence Private Walking Tour with A Tour Guide
data.description: Discover the magic of Florence on a captivating private walking tour. Led by expert guides, explore iconic landmarks like the Duomo with Brunelleschi’s masterpiece dome, Piazza della Repubblica, Piazza della Signoria, and the picturesque Ponte Vecchio. Stroll through the cradle of the Renaissance, unveiling the city’s rich history, vibrant culture, and hidden stories. Florence’s open-air beauty, combined with its artistic heritage and breathtaking sights, promises an unforgettable experience in one of the most enchanting cities on Earth.

data.name: Tour di Firenze
data.shortDescription:
Il nostro tour ti porterà alla scoperta di Firenze, culla del Rinascimento, dove passeggiando assieme alla guida locale, potrai ammirare le meraviglie della città. Passerai attraverso alcune delle più belle piazze fiorentine, come Piazza della Signoria, Piazza della Repubblica e, ovviamente Piazza Duomo.
Percorrerai anche il famoso Ponte Vecchio per godere di uno degli scorci più belli e suggestivi della città.

Pranzo e pomeriggio liberi.

data.name: Palazzo Davanzati Entrance Tickets (2)
data.shortDescription:
Also known as the Museum of the Ancient Florentine House, the Museum of Palazzo Davanzati was inaugurated as a State Museum in 1956. The 14th century palace, which was the prestigious home of the old Davizzi, merchants and bankers, its imposing façade overlooks the square of the same name, once populated by ancient tower-houses.

data.name: Florence’s dark side, a night of legends and secrets
data.description: Step beyond Florence’s Renaissance beauty and uncover its darker past on this original storytelling tour. Over two immersive hours, your expert English-speaking guide will take you on a journey through the mysteries, legends, and brutal history of Medieval Florence, a time before Michelangelo and Botticelli, when warring families and invading armies kept the city in turmoil.Your tour explores both iconic landmarks and hidden corners, revealing chilling stories rarely told. Walk across the Ponte Vecchio and through Piazza della Signoria, hearing tales far removed from those of art and architecture. At the Palazzo di Bianca Cappello, discover the tragic love story of a Grand Duke and his mistress, whose deaths were only recently explained by modern science.As you navigate Florence’s shadowy streets, learn about alleys once deemed “too dark” for safety, rooftop defences of boiling oil, and family feuds that turned deadly. Stand where traitors were burned and displayed as grim warnings to others.This Florence Night Tour reveals a city of mystery, betrayal, and intrigue, offering a captivating glimpse into its forgotten past.

data.name: Florence Combo Tour: Uffizi Gallery & City Walking Tour
data.description: Immerse yourself in the Renaissance with this combination tour of Florence's most iconic attractions. Begin with a guided exploration of the Uffizi Gallery, home to masterpieces by Botticelli, Michelangelo, and Leonardo da Vinci. Follow this with a walking tour of Florence’s historic heart, marveling at its stunning piazzas, architectural landmarks, and storied history. From the majestic Piazza del Duomo to the timeless charm of the Ponte Vecchio, this tour captures the essence of Florence's art, culture, and history.

data.name: Pitti Palace private tour and Boboli Gardens tickets
data.description: Visit Palazzo Pitti, the last residence of the Medici family, with a private guide. The palace houses paintings, ancient statues, furniture and mosaics of inestimable beauty and historical importance, not to mention the frescoes on the ceilings and walls.The tour will focus on the daily life of the Grand Dukes, from Cosimo I to the last descendants Ferdinando, Gian Gastone and Anna Maria Luisa, also known as the "Electress Palatine", to whom the museum is dedicated.Admire the extraordinary works of art belonging to the royal collection and to the families who succeeded the Medicis, from the Asburgo Lorena to the first King of Italy.In addition to the Palatine Gallery, explore the other attractions in the palace: the Royal Apartments, the Gallery of Modern Art, the Treasure of the Grand Dukes and the Museum of Fashion and Costume.At the end of the visit, the guide will give you the priority entrance ticket to the Boboli Gardens located behind the Palace, an extraordinary open-air museum populated by ancient statues, adorned with caves and beautiful fountains.

data.name: Skip-the-line skip-the-line ticket to the Uffizi Gallery
data.description: Home to the works of Michelangelo, da Vinci, Caravaggio, Botticelli and many more, the Uffizi Gallery attracts over a million visitors each year, which results in long queues, especially in high season. Save time and effort by pre-booking these priority entrance tickets, which are collected by the staff so you can avoid the queue. You will then be free to visit the gallery on your own.

data.name: From Florence: Jewels of Tuscany Tour with Lunch and Wine Tasting
data.description: Let the art cities of Tuscany seduce you with the lifestyle of their inhabitants, the beauty of their monuments and the centuries of history that exude from every stone.Enjoy the hilly Tuscan countryside on the way to Siena, the splendid medieval city worldwide renown for its artistic treasures. Visit the place where the famous Palio horse race takes place every year: Piazza del Campo with its Palazzo Comunale flanked by the tall Torre del Mangia. Spend your free time visiting the splendid Cathedral and strolling along the lively narrow streets.From Siena, take a panoramic road through vineyards and olive groves in the heart of Chianti to the ancient fortified hamlet of Monteriggioni, which was built in the thirteenth century and is still embraced by its intact walls. A short distance away, in a pleasant country estate surrounded by aromatic plants, you will be served a lunch based on typical Chianti products and a guided tasting of fine Chianti and Vernaccia wines, managed with passion and expertise by the friendly owner of the farm.After lunch, head to San Gimignano, another UNESCO World Heritage Site recognizable by the still intact medieval city structure with numerous towers hence the name "Manhattan of the Middle Ages". Discover true pieces of art such as Piazza della Cisterna, the Dome, Palazzo del Podestà and the Church of Sant' Agostino.It is finally time to reach Pisa and enjoy the sparkling sight of Piazza dei Miracoli where the peerless masterpieces in marble rise in the green lawn: the unmissable Leaning Tower, the magnificent Baptistery, the stunning Cathedral, and the Monumental Graveyard are the ultimate expression of the Romanesque architecture of the twelfth and thirteenth centuries.

data.name: Florence: A Secret Supper with House Concert
data.description: A Secret Supper with House Concert Jump into a secret world full of magic. My house is open to new friends, artists and like-minded travelers: it is a place where the passion for art, music and poetry meets the passion for good cousine. So, if you like music, good cuisine and meet new people, join me and friends of mine to enjoy the pleasure to meet each other, have a glass of wine and dinner together. We'll have a dinner based on typical Italian dishes cooked with high-quality fresh ingredients, love and research. In our idea the good food needs to be a soul cuddle. After dinner, we will experience a live music performance given by talented local professional musicians. It is the privilege of attending a secret show in a private house. Every performance has its own unique flair and what we create together will always be one of a kind. In an intimate and relaxed atmosphere, you can experience the authentic Italian art of enjoying life. So lift your wine glass, toast to love and bring with you an unique memory. Eatwith is the world's largest community for culinary experiences with locals. Savor local food and enjoy dinner parties, cooking classes and more in beautiful homes and exclusive venues. Appetizers A selection of three typical appetizers First course A typical Italian pasta dish Second course A typical Italian main course A side course Dessert

data.name: Tour guidato degli Uffizi e della Galleria dell'Accademia
data.description: Preparati a tornare indietro nel tempo all'era dell'arte rivoluzionaria e del genio maestoso del Rinascimento, non in uno, ma in due dei luoghi d'arte più amati al mondo: l'Accademia e gli Uffizi. Elena, una delle nostre esperte guide locali, afferma: "Questa è la crème de la crème delle opere d'arte rinascimentali. Esploreremo il modo in cui gli artisti di spicco hanno utilizzato la loro arte per raccontare storie importanti, con un'anteprima della vita della potente famiglia dei Medici."Preparati a rimanere a bocca aperta già alla prima tappa del tour, alla Galleria dell'Accademia: sarà come trovare uno scrigno pieno di tesori. Passeggia attraverso le sue sette sale e ammira di tutto, dai dipinti e gli affreschi nella Sala del Colosso, alle statue incompiute di Michelangelo e alle scintillanti opere gotiche dorate. Ma la vera star dello spettacolo? Di sicuro è il David di Michelangelo. Alto e orgoglioso, un colosso scolpito da un unico blocco di marmo dal genio stesso quando aveva solo 26 anni. Preparati a scattare foto come se non ci fosse un domani.Successivamente, passeggerai per Firenze fino a raggiungere la Galleria degli Uffizi: questo museo è stupefacente. Segui il tuo esperto locale sala dopo sala, ammirando le opere di leggende come Leonardo da Vinci, Raffaello, Michelangelo, Botticelli, Caravaggio e Tiziano. Avrai la possibilità di scoprire come hanno plasmato il panorama rinascimentale e il significato di questa incredibile raccolta d'arte dei Medici: verrà voglia anche a te di prendere in mano un pennello.

data.name: OT Florence Uffizi Gallery Tour with Wine tasting
data.description: TOUR HIGHLIGHTSView house paintings ranging from the 13th century to the 18th centuryWitness the famous "Madonna di Ognissanti" by GiottoPeruse an admirable creation of art by Filippo BrunelleschiTaste different wines matched with traditional Tuscan productsEnjoy the company of a charismatic guide and knowledgeable cellar staff who will educate and amuse you with local wine-making facts and storiesSample a selection of local cheeses cured meat and other types of Tuscan appetizersIf you have a special love for all that is Italian, this is a perfect tour for you. On this tour with the combination of Uffizi Gallery, you’ll be able to explore the oldest and most famous collections of art in the world at Uffizi Gallery and experience the taste of different Tuscany wines with a knowledgeable wine expert while enjoying a platter of Tuscan Appetizers.

data.name: Brunelleschi Dome & Florence Cathedral: Guided Tour + City Walking Tour
data.description:
Walk through Florence and visit famous landmarks like Piazza della Signoria. See sculptures, including a replica of Michelangelo’s *David*, and the bronze boar at Loggia del Porcellino.

Skip the line to enter the Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore. See Paolo Uccello’s clock, Vasari’s frescoes, and Bandinelli’s marble choir.

Climb to the Duomo Terraces for views of Florence’s rooftops and towers. Finish at the top of Brunelleschi’s Dome, 91 meters above the city, for views of Florence and the Tuscan hills.

data.name: Florence: Small-Group Guided Tour
data.description:
Explore Florence with a pleasant stroll through its cobblestone streets. Take in the beauty of the city's Roman origins and 15th-century palaces. Admire the historic Ponte Vecchio bridge and the beauty of the Uffizi courtyard, with Brunelleschi's Dome peeking above the "Gate of Paradise" of the Baptistery.

This walking tour offers a genuine taste of the Florentine lifestyle, enjoyed by thousands of tourists every year. With friendly local guides, embrace the allure and history of Florence for a day.

data.name: Tuscany Off-Road Winery Tour and Tasting
data.description: Exploring Chianti’s famed wine country from Florence can be a hassle, as there is little public transport and it’s easy to lose your way on the winding country roads. With this tour, set off by minivan directly from Florence, then switch to a vintage off-road 4x4 at a Chianti winery for a scenic jaunt through the rolling vineyards. After taking in the view, relax over a wine-tasting lunch at the cellar.

data.name: PRIVATE Full-Day Tour of Pisa, San Gimignano and Siena from Florence
data.description: • EXPERIENCE FOR YOUR PRIVATE GROUP • Dedicate one day to the enchanting exploration of the three best-preserved medieval cities in the world (UNESCO World Heritage sites) in Tuscany on a private day trip from Florence. Avoid the stress of renting a car or driving, and let an English-speaking private driver take you directly from the hotel door, through the scenic Tuscan countryside, and into the historic centers of Siena, San Gimignano and Pisa. Travel in premium comfort and at your own pace with invaluable advice and suggestions from your local driver. • 9/10-hr Full-Day private tour of Pisa, San Gimignano and Siena. • Pick-up and Drop-off at your Hotel or address provided. (Florence down town) • Travel in a private Mercedes-Benz Minivan. • Visit three UNESCO World Heritage sites in a single day. • Learn about the area's history and culture from a private driver.

data.name: Uffizi + David & Accademia - Priority Tickets
data.description:
Discover the most visited museums in Florence and two of the most visited in the world, admiring the most important works to appreciate the art of the Italian Renaissance. The Uffizi Gallery with its collections of works of art, masterpieces by artists and protagonists of the Renaissance such as Michelangelo, Giotto, Botticelli, Caravaggio, Leonardo da Vinci and many others.

And the Galleria dell'Accademia, the second most visited museum in Florence to discover Michelangelo's David, one of the most famous Florentine symbols. The Gallery is one of the places with the highest number of sculptures by Michelangelo, besides you can admire the museum of musical instruments, the largest collection of paintings with a gold background and the Sala dei Prigioni with sculptures designed for Pope Julius II. You will enter from the priority entrance to the museum and enjoy a journey into the life of the genius of Michelangelo.

data.name: Florence Cesarine Home Dining Experience with Cooking Show
data.description: Immerse yourself in Florentine culture and cuisine during an in-home, small-group cooking presentation with a 4-course meal. Watch how to prepare a variety of local dishes including a starter, pasta, side dish, and main course. In true Italian fashion, your meal also comes with wine and dessert.

data.name: Tuscany Group Wine Tour with San Gimignano Stop from Rome
data.description: Visit one of Italy's most famous regions, Tuscany, and sample some of its famous wines on this full-day tour from Rome. Travel through the Tuscan countryside and visit the medieval town of San Gimignano. Your tour also includes stops at two wineries where you enjoy guided tastings of Tuscan wines along with local snacks.

data.name: Wine and Dine Cooking Show in Florence with Wine Pairings
data.description:
Enjoy an exclusive culinary experience blending authentic Italian cooking with expertly paired wines. Held in Chef Vary’s elegant home or welcoming school kitchen, this event offers an intimate setting to savor Italy’s culinary traditions.

Watch and learn as Chef Vary prepares a 4-course meal using fresh, seasonal, organic ingredients. The menu changes with the season and can be personalized based on your preferences and allergies—just provide details upon booking. (You’re in Italy—be adventurous!)

Learn to make fresh pasta, ravioli, and focaccia, discover sauce secrets, and understand how to serve dishes elegantly. You can even try cooking yourself!

Each course is paired with a wine selected to complement its flavors, creating a delightful balance between food and drink.

This experience is perfect for anyone seeking a unique and relaxing evening, ideal after exploring Florence. Not suitable for gluten-free guests, vegans, or those avoiding cheese.

data.name: Opera Lirica: Auditorium Santo Stefano
data.description: In this highly-anticipated concert, hear the mellifluous sounds of opera music by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Giuseppe Verdi and Giacomo Puccini at Florence's treasured and world-renowned Auditorium di Santo Stefano al Ponte Vecchio.

data.name: Van with a view and Accademia Gallery in Florence
data.description: Experience Florence in the most comfortable way with a chauffeured minivan. This tour offers an immersive journey through some of the city's most famous landmarks, breathtaking viewpoints, and artistic treasures.Your first stop is Piazzale Michelangelo, the most famous panoramic terrace in Florence, where you can enjoy a stunning view of the entire cityscape, from the Duomo and Palazzo Vecchio to the Arno River and Ponte Vecchio. Capture unforgettable photos before heading to the nearby Basilica di San Miniato al Monte, a Romanesque masterpiece and one of the oldest churches in Florence. Admire its elegant marble façade, stunning mosaics, and the serene atmosphere that makes it a hidden gem.Next, we will drive to Fiesole, a charming Etruscan village nestled in the Florentine hills. From here, you’ll have a breathtaking panoramic view of Florence and a chance to explore the town’s rich historical heritage, including its ancient Roman amphitheater and Etruscan ruins.The final highlight of the tour is a guided visit to the Accademia Gallery, home to some of the most celebrated works of the Renaissance. Here, you’ll admire the magnificent sculptures by Michelangelo, especially the world-famous David, an icon of artistic perfection and human beauty. Your expert guide will provide fascinating insights into Michelangelo’s techniques, inspirations, and the significance of his masterpieces.

data.name: Private Tour in Florence with Electric Golf Car
data.description: Welcome to our electric golf car tour through the treasures of Florence! Discover the magnificence of the Duomo, the ancient grandeur of the Palazzo Vecchio and the incredible masterpieces of the Uffizi. Cross the romantic Ponte Vecchio, admire the sumptuousness of the Pitti Palace and immerse yourself in the serenity of Piazza Santa Croce and Santo Spirito. With us, you will explore the centuries of Florentine history and culture in a comfortable, sustainable and fascinating way. Book now for an unforgettable experience in Florence!

data.name: Wine Tasting Experience in Florence city centre
data.description:
In Florence, a few steps from the Duomo, there is a special experience going on: an exclusive Italian wine tasting experience.

Don’t miss this chance to discover and taste 3 of the best Italian wines in a traditional enoteca in the heart of Florence city center.

Daily, in an typical and traditional wine bar enoteca located in the heart of Florence a special event is going on: a Wine Tasting Experience.

Enjoy 1-hour experience, you will taste three of the most important Tuscan wines, known all around the world, such as Vernaccia di San Gimignano, Chianti Classico and Carmignano.

A sample of wine, approx 35 ml per wine, will be served with bruschette made by the Chef with local products.

During this journey throughout the winery world, a sommelier will explain to you in depth the particularity of those Italian excellencies.

Included in the experiences there are water and wine, and bruschette

Learn how to match your wine with tasty food, and how wines are made and taste with a sommelier.

data.name: Private Tour - Classic Chianti Villages & San Gimignano with Wine Tastings & Lunch
data.description: A private journey into the heart of the Chianti region along the famous Chiantigiana Road and through a classic Tuscan landscape characterized by gently rolling hills, vineyards & silver olive groves. Before leaving Florence, we will stop at Piazzale Michelangelo to enjoy a stunning view over Florence. Then, we will head to the Medieval village of San Gimignano (UNESCO World Heritage Site), famous for its 13 medieval towers which dominate the skyline. While visiting this fascinating village you will enjoy a first wine tasting. Next, we will drive along Tuscany's most beautiful country roads towards the second stage of the itinerary: Greve in Chianti. We will stop in a local winery for a second wine tasting and a traditional light lunch with typical products. Along the way, we will be stopping in other picturesque villages. The itinerary is subject to changes due to the availability of the wineries.

data.name: Florence Private Kid-Friendly Sightseeing Tour
data.description: See Florence in family-friendly style during this half-day, private tour designed with kids in mind. Play games, tackle trivia questions, and hear stories about the city’s sights. Visit San Lorenzo Market, Piazza della Repubblica, Ponte Vecchio, San Lorenzo Market, and more.

data.name: Wine tasting in Florence
data.description:
"A journey into the heart of Tuscany: 5 wines, 5 stories"

Imagine embarking on a journey through the rolling Tuscan hills, where each village holds a wine secret. With this tasting, we will take you to the discovery of five of the most famous denominations of controlled origin in Tuscany.

Accompanied by the voice of our sommelier, who will guide you on a unique sensory journey, you will taste the mineral freshness of Vernaccia di San Gimignano, the intensity of Morellino di Scansano, the elegance of Chianti Classico Gran Selezione, the complexity of Vino Nobile di Montepulciano and the structure of Carmignano.

An exclusive video, will accompany your tasting, you will see the wineries you are tasting and the sommelier will help you with the story and explanations of the wines

An unforgettable experience, for those who love wine and want to deepen their knowledge of Tuscan wine excellence in the historic Enoteca Alessi since 1952, we are number one!

data.name: Uffizi Gallery semi-private guided walking tour

data.name: Florence by Night Private Walking Tour
data.description: Take a stroll under the stars to discover the hidden secrets and shadowy corners of Florence. On this private walking tour, hear Renaissance legends and supernatural tales while wandering through romantic piazzas and dimly lit alleyways. See the city’s iconic landmarks illuminated beneath the cloak of night as you uncover a side of Florence not found in any guidebook.

data.name: Florence 3-Day All-Inclusive City Break
data.description:
Your 3-day tour from Rome to Florence and Pisa starts with a train ride that whisks you into Tuscany, one of Italy's most beloved regions. In Florence, see iconic sights like the Duomo on a guided city tour, and visit the Accademia Gallery to admire masterpieces by Michelangelo, Botticelli, and more. data.name: Florence Private Electric Mini Car Tour with Local Guide

data.name: Florence Private Tour with Uffizi and Accademia Priority Entry
