data.name: Private Shopping Tour from Florence hotels to Valdichiana Outlet
data.description:
Comfortable Roundtrip Tour from your hotel in Florence to Valdichiana Outlet Village - plays host to over 140 luxury boutiques and stores selling everything from clothes and accessories to cosmetics and home essentials. Its world-class boutiques showcasing collections from prestigious local and international designers make for a truly memorable shopping experience. Add to all these unbeatable prices, and a handful of trendy cafés and restaurants, and what you’ll get is one of the best shopping destinations in and around Florence. After you finish your shopping you will be picked up and will be delivered directly to your hotel in Florence.

All our vehicles are fully licensed and insured. We are happy to provide child seats in our cars for all ages upon request. Vehicles are clean inside and outside; our drivers are well-dressed and unfailingly attentive to our guests. They speak English. They will greet you with a name sign and will help with luggage.

data.name: Uffizi Gallery: Priority Entrance Ticket
data.description:
See the collection of statuary and busts from antiquity, previously owned by the Medici family. These ancient Roman sculptures, along with copies of lost Greek originals, are displayed in the Gallery's corridors.

Walk through time as you view the Gallery's extensive collections.

data.name: Chianti Classic Wine Tour from Florence with Transportation
data.description: In Chianti, wine is more than a business—it’s a way of life. Indulge in the good life when you book this private wine tour from Florence. This tour unveils the history, traditions, and unique qualities of the wine culture, rooted in Etruscan origins and enhanced by mineral-rich soil. Learn about the characteristics of Chianti Classico as you visit three distinct wineries for tastings of their exceptional wines.

data.name: Palazzo Pitti & Palatine Gallery: Reserved Entrance
data.shortDescription: Visit the home of the Grand Dukes of Tuscany
data.description: As Florence’s only royal palace, Palazzo Pitti is a must-see on the city’s tourist trail. It's also the largest museum complex in *The City of Lilies*; at some 32,000 m2 this is a residence fit for absolute rulers - from grand dukes to kings and emperors. The Palatine Gallery has works by Raphael, Titian, Rubens, and more. Skip the line and get into the Renaissance!

data.name: Florence Museum of Illusions (Museo Delle Illusioni) Ticket
data.description: Sometimes, you just want to take a break from art and history and culture. Bend your mind without straining your brain and capture hilarious photos for your socials when you book tickets to the Florence Museum of Illusions (Museo Delle Illusioni Firenze)—online, in advance, in the currency of your choice. Walk on the ceiling, enter into a sketch, meet your shrunken self, and more.

data.name: Skip the line: Florence Duomo Cathedral small group guided tour
data.description: Admire the magnificent Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore in the company of an expert guide.Better known as “the Duomo”, this timeless masterpiece has become the symbol of the city of Florence and Italy. You will SKIP THE LONG LINES at the entrance, saving your precious time during your vacation! Spend more time inside the Cathedral to admire the ARCHITECTURAL MARVEL of white and green marble, dominated by the imposing DOME OF BRUNELLESCHI. After skipping the line, marvel the inside of the Cathedral, with its grandiose design, illuminated by the light that passes the beautiful STAINED GLASS WINDOWS. Your local guide will take you on a JOURNEY THROUGH TIME to discover the history of the creation of the Duomo: learn about its origins as a VII century small church, to how it became the THIRD LARGEST CATHEDRAL IN THE WORLD after St. Peter’s in Rome and St. Paul’s in London. Your guide will continue to vividly recall stories of the innovative techniques used by Filippo Brunelleschi to build the ingenious Dome, which will leave you speechless. You will also be mesmerized by Zuccari and VASARI’S FRESCOES, depicting THE LAST JUDGMENT, on the most extensive surface ever decorated with this painting technique.Thanks to a preferential route reserved exclusively for our group, you can in fact access the area located below the Dome, and you can admire the marvelous fresco of the Last Judgment even closer. After the guided tour, you can stay inside the Cathedral as long as you would like to continue admiring at your own pace. The Duomo is unmissable during your holidays in Florence... Allow an expert local guide to reveal the essence of this masterpiece to you! Don't miss the chance to embark on an unforgettable adventure filled with art, history, and breathtaking views: book your tour now and let yourself be enchanted by the timeless magic of the Duomo of Florence!

data.name: Accademia Gallery: Guided Tour + Audio Guide + Skip The Line Ticket
data.description:
Avoid the long lines in Florence and head directly into the Accademia Gallery with this guided tour.

Skip the wait and start learning about famous sculptures right away.

Your guided tour in English will inform you about the history of pieces like Michelangelo's David.

Plus, enjoy pre-recorded commentary in different languages available for over twenty works, including Giambologna's _Rape of the Sabine_ thanks to the audio guide.

data.name: Florence: Accademia Gallery Michelangelo's David Evening Tour
data.description: One of the most iconic works of the Italian Renaissance—and one of Florence's top treasures—Michelangelo's David is a must-see. But the Accademia Gallery where it's housed can often be very crowded, with long waits to get in. Bypass the queues—and enjoy a less hectic time to visit—on this guided evening tour, with admission tickets included. After marveling at the larger-than-life statue, continue to other treasures many visitors skip over.

data.name: Florence Cathedral Guided Tour with Brunelleschi's Dome Access
data.description: Steer clear of the long queues and take advantage of skip-the-line access to the majestic Florence Cathedral, one of the largest cathedrals in the world and a symbol of the city, with its beautiful colorful marbles and mesmerizing geometric patterns. Reach the top of the iconic Florence Cathedral, where you'll not only marvel at the iconic architecture of Brunelleschi's Dome but also experience panoramic views of the Tuscan capital.Your guide will lead you through the Cathedral's rich history, unveiling the stories behind the Dome's construction and its enduring significance in Florence's cultural landscape. As you ascend the 463 steps, you'll gain insights into the engineering genius of Brunelleschi and the intricate construction techniques that brought this architectural masterpiece to life. This tour is a chance to engage with the history and architecture of the Duomo ensuring you a memorable experience.

data.name: Pisa and Cinque Terre Day Trip by Train from Florence
data.description: Embark on an early-day journey from Florence to Cinque Terre, Liguria's stunning seaside villages. Admire nature's artistry with steep terraces, vibrant homes and enjoy a comfortable 2-hour coach ride through Tuscany and Liguria, learning about their rich history and culture.Upon arrival, board a local train, soaking in the coastal views and fresh sea air. Explore Manarola, a picturesque town with narrow streets and a sea-view square, authentically capturing the essence of a Renaissance painting. Continue by train to Monterosso, the largest Cinque Terre town. Indulge in local dishes, stroll through charming streets, shop, or swim in the sea. Opt for a short boat tour organized by your tour leader to appreciate Cinque Terre National Park's UNESCO heritage from the sea, marveling at centuries-old residences on steep hillsides.Your next stop is Pisa, home to the Leaning Tower and other architectural wonders. See the iconic tower, with construction dating back to 1172. Conclude your tour with a quick train ride back to Florence on a private air-conditioned coach.If you want to make the most out of this Cinque Terre experience, there's an optional gentle walk, for those who want to see the stunning mainland and coastline scenery from a different perspective. As your day trip concludes, use this relaxing journey back to Florence to reflect on the extraordinary experiences.

data.name: Florence’s Uffizi and Accademia Galleries Private Walking Tour
data.description:
You’ll kick things off with a visit to the Accademia Gallery, home to Michelangelo’s iconic statue of David. Your guide is an expert on Renaissance art, so they’ll tell you the story of how the legendary artist crafted this piece, which is widely regarded to be artistically perfect. There’s a bunch of his other statues on show here, as well, along with paintings from the 15th century.

You’ll take a break from art for a bit as you make your way to the other gallery on the itinerary, the Uffizi Gallery. The journey there takes you through the Piazza del Duomo, home to Florence’s 800-year-old cathedral, and the Piazza della Signoria, where Florence’s government is based. Finally, when you reach the Uffizi Gallery, you’ll be shown around the collection, which includes work by Leonardo Da Vinci, Raphael, Caravaggio and more. All of these artists are considered masters of the Renaissance, and you’ll hear about each of their stories right up until it’s time for the gallery to close.

data.name: OT Florence Vespa Tour
data.description: TOUR HIGHLIGHTSEnjoy the freedom of the road on an original Vespa in FlorenceVisit with us to the most famous and breathtaking spot of FlorenceExplore the San Miniato convent's beautiful historic cemetery and learn about Michelangelo and the Roman historical town known as FiesoleThere is nothing more exciting than discovering Florence on board on an Italian vehicle: the Vespa. Let us fascinate and surprise you from the small Florentine streets that once welcomed only the wheels of the carriages. Explore what is around the center by immersing you in the landscapes with spectacular sightseeing spots.

data.name: Tour in Florence with Licensed Guide and Live Painting Workshop
data.description: Treat yourself to this unique and representative experience of the city of art par excellence and immerse yourself in an ancient painter! Thanks to Anna, a certified guide and professional painter, you can discover special niche places in Florence. Get away from the most crowded places of mainstream tourism! You will discover little gems that many people don't know about, admire wonderful works of art about which you will be given a variety of information, and have fun replicating their basic painting techniques in a simple and intuitive way thanks to Anna's expert guidance. Don't worry, you don't need any skills to participate in this kind of activity and it is suitable even for those who have no drawing experience at all

data.name: Chianti Day Trip from Florence: Siena, San Gimignano and Lunch
data.description:
Depart from central Florence and ride south through the Tuscan countryside by coach.

After a scenic drive past the vineyards, arrive in San Gimignano, a medieval hill town best known for its impressive towers and frescoes. Soak up some free time to explore its streets independently before heading to Monteriggioni for a short visit.

Then it's on to the charming village of Chianti for a visit to a hilltop winery. Sit down and sample fine local wines, accompanied by snacks before tucking into a 3-course Chianti-style lunch.

Finally, head to Siena and admire the Renaissance artwork inside with your guide before taking off on a walking tour. Take note of the uniquely striped marble of the Siena Cathedral and, if you've upgraded, head inside for a guided tour.

Your trip concludes with transportation back to Florence.

Please note that the order of the visits may change.

data.name: Pisa & Cinque Terre: Day Trip from Florence
data.description:
Journey from Florence to the beautiful Italian seaside, to explore the natural wonders of Liguria, home to the picturesque Cinque Terre villages.

See the terraced landscapes, local fishermen, and indulge in the region's delicacies.

Relax on a comfortable, air-conditioned coach for a scenic two-hour ride, accompanied by insightful narration about the rich history and culture. Upon arrival, board a local train for a picturesque coastal journey.

Discover the charming town of Manarola and Monterosso, the largest Cinque Terre town, where you can enjoy local cuisine, shop, or even take a refreshing swim in the sea. Optionally, enjoy a boat tour to admire Cinque Terre's UNESCO World Heritage site from the water.

Enjoy free time to explore Pisa, home to the iconic Leaning Tower.

data.name: Ferrari Museums Private Tour with Lunch from Florence
data.description: Italy’s Motor Valley and the iconic Ferrari factory and museums are located not far from Florence, but visiting by public transportation can cut into your touring time. This private full-day excursion lets you set off with a driver from your hotel in Florence. Visit both the Enzo Ferrari Museum in Modena and Ferrari Museum in Maranello. In between, savor a traditional Emilian lunch in Modena.

data.name: Florence: Accademia Gallery Reserved Timed Entry Ticket
data.description:
Don’t miss the chance to witness Michelangelo’s David up close — one of the most breathtaking masterpieces in art history.

With reserved entry to Florence’s Accademia Gallery, you’ll enjoy a hassle-free visit to this iconic museum, home not only to David but also to a stunning collection of Renaissance art. What makes this experience truly special is the included audio guide, giving you expert insights into the life, techniques, and genius of Michelangelo and other great artists. Whether you're passionate about art or exploring Florence for the first time, this self-paced tour offers a deeper, more meaningful connection to Italy’s rich cultural heritage.

data.name: Florence: Gottino Wine and Food Tour
data.description:
Get ready to eat like a true Florentine!

This authentic Gottino Tour takes you through the historic heart of Florence as we stop to savor traditional flavors, street food, and local wine — all with a local food expert by your side.

We begin with a crunchy bruschetta al pomodoro and a tasting of Tuscan olive oil and cured meats like finocchiona and prosciutto, paired with a glass of Chianti. Next, dive into Florence’s street food culture with a bold bite of lampredotto or trippa alla fiorentina — true local favorites.

To finish, enjoy a sweet Florentine treat and, of course, a stop at a wine window (buchetta del vino) for a nostalgic sip of red. Along the way, you’ll learn about the culinary history of the city, the role of food in daily Florentine life, and where locals really go to eat.

data.name: Private guided tour of Hidden Symbols in Santa Maria Novella
data.description:
Mysticism, art and hidden symbology, a special, unique and different visit.

Although the tour is designed for those people who like to understand and delve into art and its symbols, there will also be no shortage of anecdotes and curiosities.

Get ready to see beyond the obvious!

data.name: Florence: Accademia Gallery Tour with Reserved Entry Tickets
data.description: The Accademia Gallery is one of Florence’s most in-demand museums—with the lines to match. Skip the usual wait and head straight to masterpieces like Michelangelo’s David during this hour-long guided tour, which includes pre-reserved admission tickets. Choose from a range of start times, meet your guide outside, and skip the stress and hassle of trying to tackle the visit on your own.

data.name: Florence at Dawn: Early David Access + Epic Dome Climb
data.description:
This isn’t for average tourists. It’s for travelers who want bragging rights.

Start your day at the front of the line—literally. You’ll be among the first inside the Accademia Gallery, face-to-face with Michelangelo’s David, before the tour buses arrive and the crowds flood in. No noise. No chaos. Just you, the marble giant, and stories that make your spine tingle.

Next? You’ll explore the secrets of the Dome Museum and conquer Brunelleschi’s Dome—463 legendary steps, a sky-high reward, and a memory that outlives every selfie.

️ Your 3-day Duomo Complex pass also unlocks:

The Cathedral interior

Giotto’s Bell Tower

The Baptistery

The Crypt—Florence’s buried past

You’re not checking boxes. You’re unlocking Florence at its most powerful—with a local expert, a small group (max 10), and zero crowds.

⚠️ This sells out fast. Timed Dome entry. Limited spots.

Be first. Be bold. Be the traveler they wish they were.

data.name: Assisi and Orvieto Full-Day Tour from Florence
data.description:
Your tour begins in central Florence, where you hop aboard your coach with your guide and head into the region of Umbria. Stop first in the beautiful town of Assisi, made famous by its ties to St. Francis. Now known as Italy's patron saint, Francis left the wealth of his family behind in the 13th century to preach on Assisi’s streets.

Follow your guide by foot to the Basilica of San Francesco, which hosts Giotto’s famous frescoes depicting St. Francis’ life. Continue on to the Convent of Santa Chiara, dedicated to St. Clare, one of Francis’ first followers in Assisi.

Hop aboard your coach and drive to the outskirts of town to see Santa Maria degli Angeli, a 9th-century church where it’s said St. Francis came to worship. Explore the interior with your guide before making your way back to your coach.

Head next to Orvieto, perched on a cliff, for a guided tour of its town. Admire the Gothic architecture of the Duomo, with its beautiful stained glass windows, and the St. Patrick's Well.

After, travel back to central Florence to conclude your tour.

Please note: the order of the visits to Assisi and Orvieto are subject to change on the day of your tour.

data.name: Pisa and Leaning Tower Tour From Florence
data.description: A trip to Tuscany isn't complete without exploring historic Pisa, a UNESCO World Heritage site. On this round-trip driving tour from Florence, enjoy fast-track priority entry to the famous Leaning Tower, where you can climb to the top for scenic views. Your guide will also take you around Pisa Cathedral—with intricate artwork to enjoy—and some of the city's other historic sites. There's also free time to explore at your leisure.

data.name: OT Florence Accademia Gallery and Florence City Walking Guided Tour
data.description: TOUR HIGHLIGHTSAccademia Gallery skip-the-line ticket, don't waste your time queuing for the whole day!Visit the stunning sights & discover the hidden treasures of the Florence cityLearn from a passionate and art-loving local guideJoin us on a combined tour to the Galleria dell' Accademia di Firenze with a professional and friendly guide, where you will experience Michelangelo's David as well as other prominent Renaissance artworks & a walking tour to check out the highlights of the city and get the most out of your stay here in Florence.

data.name: Uffizi Gallery skip-the-line tour with local guide
data.description: With over two million visitors flocking in each year and a staggering collection of over 2,200 artworks on display, tackling the Uffizi Gallery solo can feel like diving into the deep end. But fear not – with skip-the-line tickets and a top-notch guide, this guarantees to squeeze the most out of your visit. Francesca, one of our local expert guides, says, ‘I'm here to provide the backstory behind every piece you encounter in the gallery. You'll walk away with a deeper appreciation of the collection's ties to the Medici family, Renaissance Italy, and beyond."Fully exploring the Uffizi would take days, but this tour is your golden ticket if you're short on time. You’ll head straight to the museum’s must-see masterpieces, from Leonardo da Vinci to Michelangelo, Caravaggio to Botticelli. Local guide Francesca adds, ‘when you feast your eyes on Botticelli's, 'The Birth of Venus' and 'La Primavera,' filled with goddesses, rich symbolism and dreamy colours – you’ll feel inspired. Snap up pics of these paintings that started to shape the way people saw the world.’Get ready to soak in the essence of the Uffizi as your local expert breathes life into each artwork. You'll uncover the techniques, styles, historical contexts, and symbolism behind the artists who paved the way for one of the most famous periods in art history – the Renaissance. And if you've got a combo ticket, you'll have access to the Uffizi’s temporary exhibitions too – perfect for exploring at your own pace post tour.

data.name: Pisa and Cinque Terre Full-Day Train Tour from Florence
data.description:
Your trip starts at the Santa Maria Novella train station in Florence, where you’ll meet your tour leader and group. Then relax on the train ride from Florence to Pisa.

Once there, head to Piazza dei Miracoli with your guide, where you’ll find the Duomo, the Baptistery and the Leaning Tower of Pisa. Enjoy 1.5 hours to explore independently.

Afterward, return to the train station and head toward La Spezia, switching trains to Riomaggiore, the first of five villages along the Italian Riviera that comprise Cinque Terre.

Hop off to stroll the charming streets with your guide. The buildings along each fishing village are brilliantly colored and make a stunning backdrop for your photos.

Continue by train to the village of Manarola. Check out the harbor before heading to the village of Vernazza. Here, enjoy time to explore on your own, jumping into the waters of the Riviera or taking in some rays at the beach.

Travel back to Florence by train, where your tour concludes.

data.name: Chianti: Day Trip from Florence + Wine Tour & Tasting
data.description:
Before you treat your taste buds and taste the tannins in a glass of Chianti, you'll get to feast your eyes on the rolling hills of Tuscany.

Tour a winery and hear about the winemaking process from experts. Learn how every element from soil to air and age can influence the outcome of the wine's flavor. Taste 3 local wines paired with snacks and explore the vineyards.

Round the day off with a second winery visit surrounded by Italian ambiance. Sip on an additional 3 wines with local products before heading back to Florence.

data.name: Florence: Sant'Ambriogio Local Street Food Market Tour
data.description: Head to the neighborhood of Sant’Ambrogio for a visit to a hidden gem that most tourists miss on this half-day guided food tour. Explore a local market and eat like a local as you discover street food stalls offering seasonal produce and artisanal cured meats and cheeses, and sample some traditional Italian goods at several nearby eateries.

data.name: Florence Private Walking Tour with Accademia Gallery
data.description: A great introduction to the city, this private walking tour hits several of Florence’s historic highlights. Visit Church of Santa Croce, Piazza del Duomo, the Duomo, Ponte Vecchio—a pedestrian bridge built in 1345 that is still in use today—and more. Then tour Accademia Gallery, home of Michelangelo’s masterpiece “David,” where you’ll enjoy skip-the-line access to the galleries.

data.name: Tuscany Wine & Hills from Florence
data.description: Let the rolling hills of Chianti draw you in as you explore the rich winemaking traditions in this iconic region. Visit a winery, where you’ll not only taste world-class wines but also discover the art of producing extra virgin olive oil—a blend of ancient olive varieties that captures the essence of the land. In the first cellar, you will try 3 different types of wine, so that you will understand in detail the differences in taste and texture between different bottles. Enjoy also a selection of their home-produced olive oil and Tuscan bread. Our local guides will lead you on a journey through history, art, and peasant culture, revealing the deep roots that have animated Tuscany for millennia. Next, continue your tour in the scenic Val d'Orcia, the first stop in Pienza, where architectural beauty and breathtaking landscapes create a perfect symphony. Stroll through lanes with evocative names and take in the panoramic views that have inspired poets and artists for centuries. Enjoy the free time to explore the town independently and have lunch.Carry on your trip to Montepulciano, where the grandeur of Renaissance architecture and the refined beauty of historic churches will captivate you, while the traditional Nobile di Montepulciano wine will delight your palate. Take your time to explore the city and take pictures.Your Tuscan adventure doesn’t stop there. Visit the second cellar and savor locally produced wines, including the esteemed Nobile di Montepulciano paired with traditional snacks. Conclude your day enjoying special views on your way back to Florence.

data.name: Eat Italian like an Italian
data.description:
Ciao, foodies! I'm Salvatore, your enthusiastic guide to the mouthwatering world of Florentine cuisine. If you love food as much as I do, you're in for a treat!

On our tours, we'll dive into the bustling markets, cozy trattorias, and charming artisanal shops that make Florence a food lover's dream.

So, are you ready to embark on a delicious journey through the flavors of Florence? Let's create some tasty memories together!

1. We kick things off with an iconic Florence Wine Window experience. It’s a fun bit of history.

2. We taste local salumi and cheeses with a glass of wine. Super authentic.

3. We grab classic pizza and more wine

4. We indulge in Carbonara with shaved truffles and a bold red wine. It’s a major highlight.

5. We savor pear & pecorino filled tortellini then go full Florentine with Bistecca and more wine. It’s absolutely incredible

6. We wrap things up with artisan gelato.

data.name: Florence City Hop-on Hop-off Tour
data.description: Discover Florence at your own pace aboard the iconic open-top hop-on hop-off bus! There’s truly no better way to take in the beauty of the city. Cruise through the heart of the Renaissance and hop on and off as often as you like at must-see stops like the Cathedral, Santa Croce, San Marco, Piazzale Michelangelo, and many more!Your perfect day of sightseeing, all in one ticket.Make your experience even smoother by downloading the Sightseeing Experience App: your smart companion to explore the city with ease. Inside the app, you’ll find a free walking tour of Florence’s historic center (available in 5 languages and a real-time interactive map showing where buses are, how long you’ll wait, and how to reach the nearest stop. Whether you’re planning your next stop or just soaking in the views, Florence has never been this easy to explore!

data.name: Inferno Tour - Private guided Tour in Florence
data.description: Step into the thrilling world of Inferno, the bestselling novel by Dan Brown, and follow in the footsteps of Professor Robert Langdon as you explore the stunning backdrop of Florence. This immersive tour will take you through the very places described in the book, bringing fiction and history together in one unforgettable experience.Begin at the majestic Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore, where the ancient sundial plays a key role in the story. Continue through the historic streets of Dante Alighieri’s Florence, the city of his muse Beatrice, and the poetic legacy that still lingers in every corner. The journey then leads you inside the imposing Palazzo Vecchio, where you'll step into the magnificent Salone dei Cinquecento, a hall rich in art, symbolism, and mystery.Whether you're a fan of the novel or simply intrigued by Florence’s layered history, this tour offers a unique blend of literature, legend, and breathtaking architecture.

data.name: Pasta Making Class at a 12th Century Winery in the Tuscan Countryside
data.description:
Get ready to experience Tuscany like a local with a cooking class in the middle of the Tuscan countryside at a family-run winery! Learn to make pasta just like Nonna while having fun and learning about food and wine in Florence. Explore the tastes and aromas that make Italy world-famous as you roll out your own fresh pasta! 

Departure from Florence, tour is approximately from 10am until around 3pm.

data.name: Panoramic Florence private tour on Vespa with personal photographer
data.description:
Discover the most beautiful places in panoramic Florence together with our professional photographer and our guide who will take wonderful photos of you on a Vespa at Piazzale Michelangelo, in the middle of the Rose Garden and in front of the Basilica of San Miniato.

You won't be a passive spectator, but you will be the center of attention, free to enjoy the city without impediments such as cameras and various devices.

Once the tour is over, the photographic material will be shared electronically already edited.

data.name: Florence Half-Day Italian Cooking Class with Market Visit
data.description:
Meet your chef-instructor and classmates in central Florence and head to the Central Market nearby. Step inside and meet the local vendors as you search for fresh ingredients. After gathering everything you need for your meal, walk to the cooking school.

Don your apron and get to work under the guidance of your chef, as you learn how to make a delicious Italian lunch. Prepare bruschetta, pastas such as ravioli from scratch, plus fresh sauces, and a dessert. Your chef will offer tips along the way, as well as samples from the market to nibble on.

Take a seat in the dining room once your meal is ready and toast your newfound friends with Chianti wine and feast on your creations.

With appetites and taste buds sated, depart with a diploma and a digital recipe booklet, so you can cook these dishes again for friends and family.

data.name: Chianti Tuscany Vespa Self-Drive Full-Day Tour from Florence
data.description: Explore the rolling hills, sun-blushed vineyards, and winding country lanes of Tuscany from a classic Italian Vespa. Hop aboard your own 50cc Original Piaggio Vespa scooter or share one with a friend, and follow your guide on a scenic tour of the Chianti region. Enjoy the views of the skyline of the Medieval walled city of San Gimignano, jump off to admire the views, and enjoy a delicious wine-tasting lunch at a Tuscan winery.

data.name: The art of Pasta & Wine tasting with local sommelier
data.description:
What to Expect from this Experience:

We’ll start by getting to know the ingredients. Then, you'll mix, knead, and roll your dough from scratch. Our chef will reveal secrets to perfect pasta, just like in a Michelin-star kitchen.

After cooking, enjoy your creations paired with Tuscan wines, guided by our sommelier.

Whether you're new to pasta or love wine, this is your chance to savor real Italian tradition.

How we're different:

Small group for personal attention and hands-on learning

Cook like an Italian: pasta, sauces, and ragu at the table

Authentic dishes from real chefs — not a tourist trap

Take-home recipes and a free apron to remember us by

data.name: Pisa Half-Day Tour from Florence With Skip-the-Line Option
data.description: This flexible group tour from Florence has options and upgrades that make visiting the main highlights of Pisa as easy as possible. Get dropped off right at the Piazza dei Miracoli in Pisa, then you can choose to explore on your own or upgrade to explore with a guide and get skip-the-line admission tickets to the Pisa Cathedral and the famous Leaning Tower.

data.name: Course of pasta Fettuccine and Ravioli with Truffle, Tiramisu and Wine
data.description: Roll up your sleeves and learn how to make the perfect pasta and tiramisu in a cooking class. Learn some tricks and tips on how to prepare two classic types of pasta and once you finish, you eat what you have cooked with your own hands with lots of wine to accompany. Let's start by giving a little presentation to the whole group. Follow the instructions and start preparing your fresh pasta in the traditional way all by hand, then learn the real tiramisu as it used to be, we do all this while drinking wine and having a lot of laughs. Sit down to enjoy what you have prepared and enjoy the Chef cooking it in front of you.

data.name: Skip-the-line: Uffizi Gallery Guided Tour
data.description: Meet our guide at the meeting point, where after the check-in you’ll start the guided tour of the museum. The Uffizi Gallery is one of the most famous museums in the world, and it is housed in the former “uffizi” or “offices” of the Medici Family. Your knowledgeable guide will tell you about the works of the greatest artists from the Middle Ages to the Renaissance: Cimabue, Giotto, Botticelli, Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, Raffaello, Tiziano, and many more. You will recognize original world-famous paintings you have seen in books, magazines, and on TV. You will learn about the secrets of the artists’ craft, techniques and tools. Looking at the most famous artworks of the period, you will be able to understand why Florence was the birthplace of the Renaissance. Personalize your museum experience. There is no need to rush off at the end of the tour. You may stay inside the museum until closing time.

data.name: Florence: Private Uffizi, Accademia City Half-Day Walking Tour
data.description: Discover the best of Florence's Renaissance art and architectural treasures in just half a day, all thanks to this three-in-one, private tour. Expedited skip-the-line entry to the Accademia Gallery and Uffizi Galleries helps you spend less time waiting and more time with Michelangelo's "David," Botticelli's "The Birth of Venus," and other masterpieces. Then, continue to the city center, with pauses at landmarks including the Duomo, Piazza della Signoria, and more.

data.name: Florence Sunset Small-Group Food and Wine Tasting Tour
data.description: Step into Florence’s unique food and wine scene on a tasting tour that goes beyond the usual. Enjoy 14 carefully selected Tuscan specialties and 5 expertly paired wines, including the city’s famous Negroni cocktail. Dine in comfort at three sit-down stops, experience the magic of a centuries-old wine cellar, and uncover the history of Florence’s wine windows. Uncover the city's culinary scene without having to plan a thing yourself.

data.name: Vivaldi's Four Seasons: Auditorium Santo Stefano
data.description: The Firenze Academy Ensemble will perform Vivaldi's 'Four Seasons' in the wonderful atmosphere of the Auditorium di Santo Stefano al Ponte Vecchio. The program opens with an 'Air' by Bach and Mozart's famous 'A Little Night Music'.

data.name: Palazzo Vecchio and Salone dei Cinquecento guided tour
data.description: Enjoy a two-hour guided tour of the Palazzo del Comune in Florence, the splendid Palazzo Vecchio, where the Medici family resided for centuries and where the city's political power still resides today.Wander around the beautiful and unique halls of the palace, like the Medici's private apartments, and discover the impressive artworks from the Middle Ages to Renaissance.During the visit, you will also have a chance to admire the murals that decorate the walls of the Salone dei Cinquecento. This is the largest room in Italy made for a civil power palace, built by Simone del Pollaiuolo and Francesco Domenico and commissioned by Fra Girolamo Savonarola.

data.name: Tuscan Bike Tour from Florence with Wine, Olive Oil Tastings
data.description:
Your tour begins in central Florence, where you meet up with your guide and participate in a brief safety overview before hitting the streets. Snap on your helmet and hop on your Touring bike with gears(not Electric bike, following your guide through the preserved Porta Romana gate, out of Florence.

Cycle up a 1-mile (2-km) hill, pausing to soak up the city views as you ascend. Pass the lavish villa near the top and hear the history behind the Florentine nobility whose former estates pepper the hills.

Continue through the quiet country roads, passing rolling vineyards and olive groves as you go. Learn insider facts about the region’s olive oil production from your guide as you travel.

Then treat yourself with a rest at a countryside venue and wine estate. Enjoy a glass of Chianti Classico wine and some traditional Tuscan snacks, including cheese, cold cuts, and honey.

Climb back on your bike to continue through the area’s ancient villages, stopping to spy the former home of famous astronomer Galileo Galilei.

data.name: PRIVATE Half-Day Shopping Tour: The Mall GUCCI outlet
data.description: • EXPERIENCE FOR YOUR PRIVATE GROUP • Dedicate a half-day to high-end designer shopping, update your wardrobe with new styles and current fashion trends on this shopping tour from Florence. First, start your shopping-filled day along the shops in the streets of Florence, then explore The Mall, the main outlet mall in Tuscany, with top Italian and international designer brands such as Valentino, Burberry, Gucci, Armani and many others. With an itinerary tailored to your interests, you will be able to enjoy a fun and hassle-free shopping day! • 5-Hr Half-day shopping tour of The Mall from Florence • Pick-up and drop-off at your Hotel or address provided • Visit The Mall, the largest outlet in Tuscany, buy designer products at discounted prices at Valentino, Prada, Gucci and other top brands • Travel in a private luxury Mercedes minivan (up to 8 passengers)

data.name: From Florence: Pisa and Lucca Tour with Buccellato Tasting and Optional Lunch
data.description: Both Lucca and Pisa are worldwide renowned for their incredible architecture and rich history. Delve into the art and taste of Tuscany on this informative and fun tour from Florence!Pisa is the first stop and here you will meet your knowledgeable guide: the tour starts in the incredible Piazza dei Miracoli, where you'll admire the Baptistery and the world-famous Leaning Tower before visiting the majestic Cathedral, which was completed in 1092. Pop into the local shops to buy souvenirs or stop for a quick coffee before leaving for Lucca.Famous for both the well-preserved Renaissance walls surrounding the city center and its cobblestone roads, Lucca has huge gates and impressive ramparts. Follow your guide to the enchanting old town center walking along a section of the walls and enjoying a breathtaking view over the rooftops. Anfiteatro Square, San Martino Cathedral and Guinigi Tower are the main attractions, along with a pleasant stroll through quaint streets, lined with antique shops. The tour ends with a tasting of Buccellato, a typical Lucchese cake filled with sultanas, raisins and aniseed - the perfect end to a perfect day! The Lucchesi people say that if you visit Lucca and don’t eat some Buccellato, then you haven’t really been there!You can also choose to add a typical Tuscan lunch, which includes an appetizer, a first course, dessert, water and wine: the best conclusion for this unforgettable experience!

data.name: The other side of Florence food guided tour
data.description: Experience the heart and soul of Florence through its culinary traditions on this immersive 4-hour walking tour of the Oltrarno neighborhood. As you stroll through the charming historic streets, you'll discover the neighborhood's rich history and vibrant food culture.This tour offers five unique food and drink tastings, from succulent cured meats to creamy gelato, each carefully selected to showcase the best of Tuscan cuisine. You'll have the opportunity to taste local favorites that have been passed down for generations, all while hearing the stories behind the dishes from your knowledgeable guide. But it's not just about tasting the food – you'll also have the chance to learn about the cooking techniques and traditions behind them. At a local restaurant kitchen, you'll witness a cooking and baking demonstration that will give you an insight into the secrets of Tuscan cuisine.And no food tour of Florence would be complete without meeting the artisans who create the city's most beloved dishes. You'll have the opportunity to interact with these skilled craftsmen and women, learning about their passion for food and their commitment to preserving traditional techniques. This tour is perfect for foodies and culture lovers alike, offering a unique and authentic glimpse into the heart of Florence's culinary scene. So join us on this unforgettable adventure and discover the delicious flavors of the Oltrarno neighborhood!

data.name: Sunset Chianti Tuscany Wine Tasting Tour from Florence
data.description: Immerse yourself in the quiet Tuscan countryside on this small-group wine-tasting tour. Indulge in the region’s famous wine and food while admiring the landscape. Begin in Greve in Chianti, exploring its lively square and artisan shops. Continue to Panzano, where a charming 12th-century church and picturesque hills await. Enjoy a farmhouse lunch featuring homegrown produce, wine, and olive oil, and stop at Piazzale Michelangelo to snap some photos of the Florence skyline.

data.name: Florence Accademia: Michelangelo’s David Skip-the-Line Tour
data.description:
With this tour of Florence’s Galleria dell‘Accademia, you have the benefit of choosing between multiple start times from morning to late afternoon, making it easy to fit into your schedule.

Meet your guide in Piazza delle Belle Arti—look for a sign with the name “Florence with Elvis Guided Experience.” Pay for your priority entrance ticket with the help of your guide and bypass the long lines and the crowds struggling to enter the museum.

Put on the radio transmitters provided by your guide to better hear the tour narration, and head inside. Explore the museum and make your way to Michelangelo’s “David,” discovering the sculpture and other highlights up close.

Benefit from your guide’s insider knowledge by listening to her narration.

After about one hour in the museum, end your tour in Piazza delle Belle Arti.

data.name: Pisa Skip-the-Line Tower of Pisa Afternoon Tour from Florence
data.description:
Your day trip will begin in central Florence, where you’ll hop on your air-conditioned coach and relax on the ride to Pisa. Watch the scenery change from bustling Florentine streets to the vineyards and rolling hills of the Tuscan countryside.

Upon arrival in Pisa, explore Cathedral Square (Piazza dei Miracoli) with your guide. Admire the impressive Duomo, Baptistery, and Camposanto Monumentale as your guide provides insightful commentary on the historic sites around you.

Gaze up at the impressive Palazzo Vescovile in Piazza Arcivescovado, now a popular hotel.

Make your way to the city’s most famous monument, the Leaning Tower of Pisa, and bypass the lines with your direct access ticket. Head straight up the spiraling 294 steps to admire panoramic views at the top.

After the guided tour, you will have some free time at your disposal to explore. Your tour will conclude with transportation back to Florence.

Please note: If you have no head for heights, walking difficulties or aversion to enclosed spaces, the Leaning Tower of Pisa climb probably won’t be for you. Use the time to relax at leisure in Cathedral Square, instead.

data.name: Florence: Panoramic view Brunelleschi's Dome Guided Tour
data.description: Join this small-group tour to climb Brunelleschi’s Dome, or the Duomo, for some excellent views of Florence. Listen to your audio guide and learn all about the history of the architecture, the art, and the creators. Take your time touring the area, and spend time admiring the fresco The Last Judgment, by Giorgio Vasari.

data.name: Uffizi Gallery guided tour from Motecatini
data.description: Start your day in Montecatini and take the train to Florence (tickets are included and will be sent by email).. Upon arrival in Florence meet our guide at the meeting point in front of Uffizi Gallery - Entrance tickets n.3 , where after the check-in you’ll start the guided tour of the museum. The Uffizi Gallery is one of the most famous museums in the world, and it is housed in the former “uffizi” or “offices” of the Medici Family. Your knowledgeable guide will tell you about the works of the greatest artists from the Middle Ages to the Renaissance: Cimabue, Giotto, Botticelli, Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, Raffaello, Tiziano, and many more. You will recognize original world-famous paintings you have seen in books, magazines, and on TV. You will learn about the secrets of the artists’ craft, techniques and tools. Looking at the most famous artworks of the period, you will be able to understand why Florence was the birthplace of the Renaissance. Personalize your museum experience. There is no need to rush off at the end of the tour. You may stay inside the museum until closing time. After the tour make your way back to Montecatini on the train.

data.name: Semi-private Accademia Gallery and Walking tour of Florence
data.description: The first part of the tour starts right in front of the main entrance of the Accademia Gallery where with our knowledgeable guide you will learn why David is the most recognizable symbol of Florence and what it used to represent in his time. How did the genius of Michelangelo meet the challenge of extracting the pathos of a being and fixing it forever in time in the Pietà or the famous Prisoners who still seem to struggle free from their marble blocks? You will have the answers to all your questions. Get the chance to have a close encounter with timeless works of art and get the inside story of the life and times of this consummate artist. After the guided tour you will have some free time to wander around on your own and some free time to have lunch (not included). The second part of the tour includes a walking tour in which you will enjoy an excellent and complete introductory tour dedicated to those who want to know all the facts and secrets of two thousand years of Florentine history, from the city’s Roman origins to a 15th-century palace, including the Ponte Vecchio, the famous Uffizi courtyard, and the wonders of the architecture of Brunelleschi’s Dome which overlooks the Baptistery golden ‘Gates of Paradise.

data.name: Historical Whodunit in Florence - Murder Mystery Self-Guided Tour
data.description: Would you like to explore the streets of Florence city center whilst solving a murder mystery case? You get the facts of an actual Renaissance murder, then you conduct the investigation by following provided clues on a hunt to unmask the criminal from the list of possible suspects. On this self-guided tour, where Florence is the protagonist, you will visit both known and less known sites in the city to uncover the information you need to solve the crime.  But take a close look at the sites on the itinerary or you might miss a crucial evidence! The magnifying glass and deerstalker hat are optional!

data.description: This tour will take you admiring the monuments that symbolize old Florence with a local guide, and discovering the masterpieces that created the culture of our time.Visit the Accedemia Gallery to admire the David as well as other great works by Michelangelo. Along the way, you will admire the marvelous Duomo complex with its monuments completely covered in poly chromatic marble, such as the great dome by Brunelleschi, the Baptistery and the Campanile by Giotto. You'll then proceed to the imposing and outstanding stone building of the Church of Orsanmichele, home to Orcagna's wonderful Gothic tabernacle. Continue to the lively Mercato della Paglia, with the famous "piglet", and reach Piazza della Signoria, home to sculptural masterpieces of Loggia dei Lanzi, and the imposing Palazzo Vecchio with the crenelated tower of Arnolfo.Finally, enjoy a unique perspective of Palazzo degli Uffizi, which opens up to the square. data.name: The Four Seasons by Antonio Vivaldi in Florence
data.description: Music that captures the changing moods of the four seasons has long captivated audiences, with baroque composers like Werner and Fischer creating concerto cycles inspired by the seasons. Yet none depicted such vivid imagery as Antonio Vivaldi in his celebrated Four Seasons concertos. Throughout the Baroque period, there was a profound fascination with the wondrous transformations brought about by the seasons. Artists like Bernini captured these themes in intricate sculptures. Baroque art portrayed a dramatic interaction between humanity, nature, and the cosmos. Galileo's breakthroughs redefined humanity's place in the universe, sparking a new sense of admiration and respect for nature's might. Vivaldi’s Four Seasons epitomizes his time, rendering awe through his vivid nature portrayals and innovative musical expression. He astounds listeners with unique melodies, dynamic rhythms, and heightened harmonic contrasts. His music flows freely and vividly narrates its story, from spring's bird songs to summer storms, from autumn's fleeing foxes to winter's chattering teeth and pouring rain. In true baroque fashion, nature is dramatized, engaging audiences in its swift sequence of events. Experience the immersive power of Vivaldi's Four Seasons at Florence's Teatro Niccolini, a landmark of Italian Baroque music performed by the Opera e Lirica Academy string quintet and harpsichord. Violin soloist and Conductor: Elvin Dhimitri Strings Quintet Harpsichord TEATRO NICCOLINI Florence's Niccolini Theater, Europe's first 'modern' theater, dates back to the mid-1600s, crafted by nobles in Palazzo Ughi on via del Cocomero. Artists like Vittorio Gassman, Carmelo Bene, and Paolo Poli graced its stage in the 1970s and 1980s. Its 2016 restoration ushered in a vibrant artistic era, offering an array of plays, concerts, and cultural events annually.

Visit a family-run winery, where you'll enjoy a wine tasting paired with a delightful light lunch featuring authentic Tuscan flavors. Afterward, explore the medieval streets of San Gimignano, known for its stunning towers and world-renowned gelato. data.name: Guided visit and skip-the-line tickets to the Uffizi Gallery
data.description: You can't leave Florence without visiting one of the most famous art galleries in the world. Here you can admire numerous works of art by Botticelli, Michelangelo, Leonardo da Vinci, Raffaello, Giotto, Cimabue, Masaccio and many others.Among the exhibition halls of the Gallery, the most renowned one contains the refined works by Botticelli, among which two masterpieces: "Primavera" and "Birth of Venus". The latter painting, the icon of the museum, represents the allegory of the birth of the goddess emerging from the sea foam and symbolizes the ideal of beauty as an expression of purity and spiritual quality, typical of Renaissance Neoplatonic aesthetics.The guided Tour ends at the Uffizi Terrace where you can enjoy an amazing and exclusive view of the city’s most important monuments.Once the guided tour is over, it is possible to stay in the museum.

data.name: Pisa and Piazza dei Miracoli Half-Day Tour from Florence
data.description: Have you ever wanted to climb all the steps up to the top of the Leaning Tower of Pisa? Well, this half day tour from Florence gives you the opportunity to enjoy the city of one of the symbols of Italy. We start our excursion with a walk along side the Medieval walls up to the old entrance gate: Porta Santa Maria. From here an extraordinary view will take your breath away! You will be in front of a unique panorama: Piazza dei Miracoli with its marble architecture and neat grass lawns. Your guide will accompany you on your visit to the precious interiors of the Cathedral, an unchallenged masterpiece of Romanesque art. Once outside you can admire the Baptistery, the Monumental Graveyard and, finally, the world famous LEANING TOWER, discovering all its secrets. Selecting the optional admission ticket to the Leaning Tower, you don't just see the Tower but you also get to climb up it without waiting and queuing. Before heading back to Florence you will have free time for an ice-cream and for the inevitable photo -memories.

data.name: Boboli Garden: Fast Track Entry + Guided Visit + Florence Walking Tour
data.description:
Visit Boboli Garden in Italy with a professional guide. Designed by Niccolò Tribolo and other artists, it’s one of the country's oldest landscaped gardens.

Start at the courtyard of Pitti Palace. Walk to the "Artichoke" Fountain and the Amphitheatre. See Neptune’s Fountain and the "Abundance" statue by Giambologna.

Walk down the Viottolone, a path lined with cypress trees, leading to the Isolotto pond and its "Ocean" Fountain, also by Giambologna.

See the "Giardino del Cavaliere," Michelangelo’s work, the Kaffeehaus, and the Buontalenti Grotto.

In the afternoon, take a guided walk from Piazza della Repubblica to Piazza del Duomo. Visit Palazzo Vecchio, see Michelangelo’s David, and visit the Uffizi Gallery.

End at Ponte Vecchio and Palazzo Pitti, learning about Florence’s landmarks along the way.

data.name: Florence Renaissance Secrets and Scandals Guided Walking Tour
data.description:
Your tour begins in Florence's historic center by Piazza Davanzati. Following your knowledgeable guide, explore hidden side streets and hear stories of this illustrious city's shadowy past, when the world's oldest profession was the backbone of Florence's economy.

Learn how certain street addresses in Florence once distinguished lower-class from upper-class courtesans. Hear about how some of the city's most revered citizens were involved in some of the most sordid events of the Renaissance era. Find out what's behind the seemingly odd names of various streets in the historic center.

Along the way, you'll visit the Piazza del Duomo with its famous bapitstery and bell tower, the Piazza della Repubblica, a palace that was home to the ruling Medici family, and the Bargello. Today, the Bargello is an art museum, but its dark history is that it was once a jail.

You'll find out what strange concoctions Renaissance citizens believed had healing properties and see a well where they once dumped the deceased — a place locals still prefer to avoid!

data.name: Uffizi private guided tour with an art historian in Florence
data.description: Florence’s Uffizi Gallery is one of those rare places that lives up to the hype. And, while its epic queues put some visitors off, it’s not a worry for you with your skip-the-line entrance. Your expert guide will thoughtfully steer your group through the collection during a private tour. Valentina, a local art historian and guide, says, “it’s impossible to stop and appreciate all 2,200 pieces, but I love to show off a few of my favourites, alongside some more unusual pieces, like Bandinelli’s 2,000-year-old statue.”The Uffizi is home to the world’s largest collection of Renaissance paintings, but it was first commissioned as a place of business in 1560 by a member of the influential Medici dynasty. Valentina adds, “as you wander its 96 opulent rooms, you’ll hear stories and secrets about the mighty Medici family that you won’t find in the guidebooks.”It’s a feast for the eyes, as you take in all the must-see masterpieces, from Botticelli’s The Birth of Venus, to Da Vinci’s Annunciation and the Giotto room, displaying the Uffizi’s oldest paintings. Scatterings of Michelangelo, Caravaggio and Raphael across the gallery will fight for your attention, while your guide keeps order and helps you absorb the context, symbolism and quality of each piece. The tour ends with a well-deserved break at the terrace café. But, if you’re still keen to explore more, or just have to revisit a favourite, you can wander to your heart’s content, as your ticket is valid until closing time.

data.name: San Gimignano, Siena and Chianti Tour - Small Group

data.name: Discover Florence in a Day: Private Full-Day Walking Tour
data.description: Explore the best of Florence, the beautiful capital city of Tuscany on this full-day private tour with an expert guide. The birthplace of Dante and Michelangelo and ruled by the infamous Medici family, Florence is often called the Cradle of the Renaissance and is an open-air museum of beautiful Renaissance architecture, statues and monuments, cobbled streets, hidden gems down little-known side streets, world-famous galleries, sunny piazzas, gorgeous old bridges, and wonderful vistas. On your private tour, you will:  Meet your guide outside the Hotel Minerva opposite the stunning facade of Basilica Santa Maria Novella, which lends its name to the train station nearby; Walk to the famously vibrant San Lorenzomarket, the indoor market selling fresh food and local produce, the lively outdoor market famous for its leather, pottery, and other souvenirs;  See the famous Medici church and mausoleum the Basilica di San Lorenzo from the outside, one of the largest and oldest in Florence, designed by many leading architects including Brunelleschi, Donatello, and Michelangelo;  Walk to the iconic Piazza Del Duomo in the heart of Florence, dominated by the Basilica of Santa Maria del Fiore with Brunelleschi’s famous dome, Giotto's Campanile, and the Baptistry; Learn all about these buildings, the architects, and the scandalous Pazzi conspiracy;  Head to central Piazza della Repubblica to hear about Italy’s Risorgimento, and on to the Mercato del Porcellino where you’ll learn about the Florentine leather tradition which dates back to antiquity, and how the Florentines used the Arno river in the production process; Pass by Dante’s House, and learn all about the life and work of this seminal Italian writer, famous for his epic poem The Divine Comedy;  Explore the Santa Croce neighbourhood with the grand Basilica di Santa Croce at its heart - where Michelangelo is buried; Enjoy a leisurely and well-deserved lunch break at a local restaurant (not included);  Walk to Piazza dell Signoria with its impressive, muscular marble statues including a replica of David, and the Palazzo Vecchio the historic political centre of Florence; Admire the elegant Uffizi Gallery buildings, a prime example of 16th-century Italian architecture; Walk over the famous Ponte Vecchio, uniquely lined with shops it was the only bridge over the Arno river until 1218, and see if you can spot the secret Vasari Corridor; See the grand exterior of the Renaissance Pitti Palace, once the official residence of the Medici Family; Visit the magnificent Basilica of Santo Spirito, one of the best examples of Renaissance architecture by the famous architect Filippo Brunelleschi (who designed the extraordinary dome of the Duomo among many other achievements) ; Explore the Oltrarno district, Florence’s coolest neighbourhood, known for its artisanal shops and many bars and restaurants, a favourite hangout for the locals; Enjoy a delicious Gelato on us at your guide's favourite gelateria! Florence sits serenely on the Arno River in the heart of Tuscany and is known for its Renaissance beauty everywhere you look. On your private tour of this Renaissance city, home to some of the greatest names of all time from Michelangelo to the Medici, you’ll explore all the most notable highlights, including the Duomo, with Brunelleschi’s Dome, which took 140 years to complete, and the Baptistry of St John, built over 70 years and named after the Saint Protector of Florence- San Giovanni. You’ll hear all about the lives, accomplishments, and scandals of the families and artists that made Florence, as you wander the quaint cobbled streets, gazing at magnificent buildings, glorious piazzas and spectacular statues.Admire views of the Ponte Vecchio and the Arno, and hear about life in modern Florence as you walk through the vibrant markets that have been going since medieval times, and end with an orientation around the trendy Oltrarno area, filled with artisanal shops and lively bars. Enjoy a delicious gelato with your guide who will be happy to help you with dinner/shopping/sightseeing recommendations. Please note that there is often a long line to enter the Duomo of Florence. If the line is too long you will not visit the interior of the Cathedral on tour, and your guide will give you tips on the best time to return to avoid standing in line.

data.name: Private Tour - A Day in the Enchanting Val D'Orcia with Wine Tasting
data.description: During this private full-day tour in a comfortable air-conditioned minivan, you will explore the enchanting Val D'Orcia, a renowned region in the south of Tuscany. The wonderful landscapes of this region will take your breath away, as well as its characteristic villages. We will visit the Medieval hill town of Montepulciano, located in the province of Siena and sitting high on a 605-metre limestone ridge. Montepulciano is known worldwide for its wine and typical products: we will enjoy a tasting of wine and local products right in this picturesque location. Our tour will continue to Pienza, another exquisite town located in Val D'Orcia, widely known as the "ideal city of the Renaissance". Pienza was realized by the request of Pope Pius II (Enea Silvio Piccolomini). He wanted to transform his native town, the humble Corsignano, into what he considered the perfect Renaissance city should be, following the principles and the philosophy of classical times. The rebuilding was done by Florentine architect Bernardo Rossellino, under the guidance of the great humanist and architect Leon Battista Alberti. Along the journey, there will be plenty of occasions for photo stops.

data.name: Italian Beef Experience Chianina Cooking Class
data.description: The True Tuscan Beef Italian Cooking ClassWhen it comes to food, Italy is the place to visit. No matter if you are a beginner or if you are an experienced cook, willing to prepare your next menu. Italy, and more specifically Tuscany, can offer you a wide range of opportunities regarding learning how to become a master chef. Join us in the heart of Florence to take part in an original cooking class that will make you able to prepare a full Italian meal. We will start from the basics, learning about quality raw food and how to maintain its sweetness and vital liquids. Then we will go deeper into recipes, like that of meat tartare, florentine steak, grilled vegetables, and worldly-appreciated tiramisu.What you will get with this Italian Cooking ClassStop making it difficult. There are different kinds of meals being part of the Italian cooking tradition. In the beginning, you don’t need to start from the pasta making class. Learning what is the Italian approach towards flavor is essential. Italian cooking is not just about learning how to execute recipes. It is a mental approach that leads us to use our senses to get in touch with fats, spices, raw meats, and vegetables. At the beginning, in order to warm up, you will be served a glass of wine and a Tuscan typical starter. The lesson will start with a proper introduction to the Italian most famous breed of cattle.What does Chianina mean?The Chianina Beef, alongside the Piemontese, is without any doubt one of the best Italian beef varieties to be grilled. We will start describing the Chianina, the big white cow, a special breed of cattle that have been selected during centuries for its resistance during plowing and work in the countryside. Due to this particular history, the Chianina breed developed a huge muscle mass, that later defined its culinary success. Defended and promoted by a specific Protection Consortium (Consorzio di Tutela del Vitellone Bianco dell’Appennino Centrale), the Florentine steak made mandatorily with Chianina beef is low-fat meat, rich in flavors. In this cooking class, you will be introduced to the different cuts, being aware of the differences between steaks, Florentine bone steaks, t-bone steaks, and how cultural habits reflect on the preparation and the grilling phase.Take part in a unique Florentine Beef ExperienceFirst, you’ll learn how to prepare the famous meat tartare, dicing it properly with a knife. At the end, you’ll gain your Meat Cutter Diploma that you’ll be able to frame and show proudly back at home. Then, you’ll be trained to the Florentine bone-steak preparation, involving marinade, cutting, seasoning, and serving. Then it will come the time for grilled seasonal vegetables, how to cook them preserving their nutritional properties and what is the best dressing.The original Tiramisu Recipe and two special giftsThis special Italian cooking class will finish with the original tiramisu recipe. Tiramisu is one of the most famous icy Italian desserts, appreciated worldwide by kids and adults. Even if its ingredients are few and the preparation process may seem to be simple, the secret of this genuine Italian dessert relies on the traditional gestures and knowledge stored by the Italian nonnas (Italian grandmothers).Finally, you will be invited to sit down and relax, tasting the Florentine steak and the grilled vegetables you have prepared, alongside a glass of good Chianti red wine. As a gift, in addition to the diploma, you will receive a trendy apron and a chef's bandana.

data.description: Explore the crown jewel of Florence inside and out on this ultimate Duomo tour including a climb to the top of the cupola for magnificent views of the city and grand cathedral below. Learn the history of Brunelleschi's medieval feat of engineering, and admire the original baptistery "Doors of Paradise" and other Renaissance relics on a guided tour of the Opera del Duomo Museum.

data.name: Florence Local Traditional Food Walking Tour
data.description:
Discover a different side to a city on an immersive food walk and market tours. Our local hosts will show you all their favorite places to eat, drink and have fun!

This Florence Food tour is the perfect way to learn more about the city and it's food! Italian cuisine is loved across the globe and the choices can be overwhelming. During this tour, your guide will select the most famous Tuscan delicacies from meats and cheeses, to homemade pasta, plant based dishes and sweet pastries. Come along to satisfy your appetite as well as your interest in Florence and its history!

data.name: Tour of the Mysteries and Legends of Florence
data.description:
Florence has been the usual scene of numerous conspiracies, plots and murders that have marked the course of history. At night, memories begin to emerge in a city whose past was not always linked to the artistic idealism of the Renaissance...

To delve into the mysteries and legends of the capital of Tuscany, we will find ourselves in front of the church of Santa Maria Novella. There we will tell you how the Black Death affected the city during the 14th century.

We will visit the oldest pharmacy in the world, we go to the baptistery where we talk about the column of Saint Zenobius and the last miracle, then we go to the Cathedral Baptistery where we will learn about the dome sphere because it has fallen in the past, then we go to the Dante's church Piazza della Signoria Vassariano Corridor that connects the Palazzo Vecchio with the Uffizi and we finish the tour of the mysteries and legends of Florence in the Veo Pontecchio.

data.name: Florence Small-Group Express Walking Tour
data.description: Florence is nicknamed an “open-air museum” for a reason—it’s packed with attractions. Ideal for travelers with limited time to spare, this one-hour small-group tour ticks off many of the highlights. Learn about the Renaissance city’s famous art, architecture, and history as you see sights like Ponte Vecchio, Piazza della Signoria, and Florence Cathedral, aka the Duomo, all in a group of just eight travelers maximum.

data.name: OT Florence Promo Duomo Complex Italian Guided Tour w/ Cupola Entry Tickets
data.description: After seeing the Duomo Complex from all sides by joining a guided tour with local expert guides, all you need to do to complete the experience is climb to the top of the dome. See the entire city from a single point by climbing to the top of Florence's Dome.Tour HighlightsEnjoy a spectacular view of the cityClimb to the top of the Cupola, the highest point in FlorenceSee an admirable creation of art by Filippo Brunelleschi

data.name: Florence Private Walking Tour With A Professional Guide
data.description: Florence is all about the Italian renaissance and the events that shaped the its history. Come on a journey from its roman origins to the 15th century, including the church of Santa Croce, the resting place of many of the illustrious like Michelangelo and Galileo. We will see legendary attractions like the Pallazo Vecchio, the old city hall of Florence, the Mercato Nuovo, the 16th Century covered market hall, the Loggia dei Lanzi and it’s 10 renaissance statues and the Ponte Vecchio over the Arno river. You will be astonished by the sculptures at the patio in the Galeria degli Uffizi and marvel at the Santa Croce church. In the end of the tour will take you to observe the dome of Brunelleschi at the monumental cathedral of the Duomo and get up close for a peek at the doors of the Baptistery. Following the footsteps of the artists, we will find out more about the cradle of the renaissance, and get to know as well the modern side of town, for a later exploration on your own.

data.name: Florence Local Fashion Designers Shopping Tour with a Stylist
data.description: Explore Florence’s fashion scene and local designers with a private shopping tour guided by a professional stylist. data.name: Family-Friendly Florence—Private Guided Walking Tour
data.description: Many tours of Florence are too historical and dry for children. Don't spend your vacation struggling to play tour guide to the kids—join a Florence native and licensed tour guide on this fun sightseeing tour packed with kid-friendly anecdotes about the people and secrets of the Renaissance. Cross the Ponte Vecchio; admire the Duomo, Giotto's Bell Tower, and the stripy facade of the Basilica of Santa Maria Novella; and more.

data.name: Uffizi Gallery Small Group Tour: Discover Uplifting Masterpieces
data.description: The Uffizi Gallery is one of Italy’s most visited museums, home to masterpieces by Botticelli, Raphael, and Da Vinci. data.name: Florence Private 2-Hour Artisan Workshop Visit in Oltrarno
data.description: Florence is known for its traditional craftsmanship, but it’s easy to get swept up in tourist traps. Dodge the crowds and head to the under-the-radar neighborhood of Oltrarno during this exclusive visit to three artisan workshops. Step inside a marbled paper studio, a family-owned leather workshop, and a mosaic laboratory. You’ll even get a chance to make your own take-home souvenir.

data.name: Tuscany: Private Tour of Pisa, San Gimignano, and Chianti
data.description: Discover Tuscany at its finest in one day, with historical towns, breathtaking views, and stunning art. Avoid transport hassle with a private driver, who will whisk you through beautiful countryside to the historic towns of Pisa, San Gimignano, and Chianti. Learn about the area's culture and see the famous Leaning Tower of Pisa. Experience wine being produced in the renowned Chianti region, with the option for lunch and a tasting of six wines (own expense).

data.name: Exclusive Cortona tour from Florence: Land of Tuscan Syrah.
data.description:
On the border between Tuscany and Umbria lies one of the prettiest, charming and historical towns in Italy; Cortona. Cortona is enclosed by ancient stone walls dating back to Etruscan and Roman times.

Known for its picturesque landscapes and the film "Under The Tuscan Sun", this medieval town is also supposedly the birthplace of the founder of Troy (Dardano), whose descendants eventually left Troy and founded Rome!

But what many do not know is that this town is also home of the most delicious wines in Italy.

Discover Cortona and its wines in a private Tour, through a meticulously curated guided wine tasting experience showcasing the winery’s finest creations. The DOC wines of Cortona are renowned for their high quality and unique flavors, with a wide range of styles and flavors, there is something for every wine lover to enjoy. The wines of Cortona are sure to Impress.

Enjoy a lunch prepared inside the winery and paired with the winery’s best wines.

data.name: Skip-the-line guided tour of the Uffizi Gallery for small groups
data.description: The Uffizi Gallery ranks high on the list of any art-lover visiting Florence, a fact that regularly results in general access lines stretching for hours... Join this one hour and a half guided tour with skip-the-line tickets to save precious time and get the best from your visit! This tour has been perfected during the years in order for you to be able to admire all the highlights of the Gallery, whose entire collection would be impossibile to see in one day only. It will allow you to admire Botticelli’s iconic work "The Birth of Venus" and Leonardo da Vinci’s "The Annunciation" to name but a few. You will also have the opportunity to learn more about the Gallery itself, which was started by Giorgio Vasari in 1560. Yor guide will provide you with all the necessary insights about the Uffizi and its works of art.This will be a small group experience, with a maximum of 9 people per group, and audio headseats for everyone. Your tickets will then be valid for the rest of the day, so, if you'd like, you could also stay and explore more of the Uffizi.

data.name: Heart of Umbria region: explore the mystic towns of Orvieto and Assisi
data.description: Let’s head to the heart of Umbria and explore the medieval town of Orvieto and the city of Assisi, which lies at the foot of Mount Subasio.Orvieto rises on a tuff cliff and perfectly combines history, art and natural beauties. Marvel at the grandeur of the gothic architecture of the Duomo, whose facade is enriched by precious mosaics and sculptures that will take you to another world. Don’t miss the chance to visit also the inside of the church, with its colorful stained-glass windows and one the most famous frescoes of Luca Signorelli (please, note that the entrance ticket to the Duomo is not included in the price of the tour).Another major attraction of Orvieto is Saint Patrick’s well: a true engineering masterpiece designed to provide a reliable water supply during sieges. Access the depths of the well with the two helical ramps and find yourselves right into another dimension (please, note the entrance tickets to the well are not included in the price of the tour). Get lost among the narrow alleys, explore the local squares and enjoy the typical medieval architecture of the buildings. Don’t forget to browse around the numerous artisans’ workshops: take the chance to bring home a unique artifact to remember forever the time spent in Orvieto.After some free time, you will get back on our fully-fitted GT Coach and head to Assisi: one of Umbria’s most fascinating borgo. Assisi is the city of the Saints: Saint Francis and Saint Clare. It lies on top of a hill, once called Hill of Hell, “Colle dell’Inferno”, since it used to be the burial site of those who were condemned to death. They then changed its name to Hill of Paradise once they set the first stone of the Basilica of Saint Francis.An expert local guide will lead you through the secrets of the city while you walk through its steep winding alleys. You will then enter the famous Basilica of Saint Francis, home to some of the best preserved frescoes painted by Giotto, Pietro Lorenzetti, Simone Martini and Cimabue. You will then enter also the Basilica of Saint Clare, one of the first followers of Saint Francis and founder of the Order of Poor Ladies. After the guided tour, you will have some free time to go shopping in the local small stores or to just chill in the main square, sipping a good coffee.The last stop of the trip before eventually going back to Florence will be the Papal Basilica of Saint Mary of the Angels: a majestic church built on top of the Porziuncola, a smaller church where the Franciscan movement originally started.

data.name: Chianti: Half-Day Winery Tour and Tasting From Florence
data.description: Chianti is one of the world’s most celebrated wine-making regions, but getting around can be a challenge without private transportation. Enjoy a hassle-free visit during this shared coach tour from Florence. Enjoy free time to explore its scenery. Then, head to a winery for a behind-the-scenes tour and additional wine tasting, accompanied by Italian “slow food” delicacies.

data.name: Hike & Taste Experience in Siena from Florence
data.description: Staying in Florence is amazing, but if you're looking for an extraordinary day off and you don't have a car, this experience is exactly what you were looking for. From Flornce main train station this morning you get a train at 8.10 am in order to reach Siena. You will arrive at the Siena Train Station by 9.45 am. From here you start your walking tour towards the winery which is only 2 miles away; you have a splendid walking tour and reach it by 11.30 am, when the wine tour starts!  At your arrival you'll meet a member of the family for the vineyard tour. "Environment before business, People before brand, Substance before shape", this is the claim and philosphy of this winery! During the visit to the ORGANIC vineyards you will go through all the main steps of the agronomic, phenolic and organic cycle in order to understand the complexity of the “vineyard” ecosystem and of an agriculture with low environmental impact.  You will then move to our historical cellar where we will discover the chemical-physical and microbiological processes that make a quality production. and then continue the journey moving to the sensorial tasting room to grasp the organoleptic complexity of their wines and have a better understanding of them. The visit will end up with a light-lunch to experience the emotions that the right combination food/wine can offer to our palate and to our spirit! At the end of the experience you have different options, considering than the train is booked at 7.15 pm: - You may want to walk back and reach Siena to visit the downtown of the city - You can call a taxi to go to Piazza del Campo and then reach the station Remember, the train will depart at 7.15 pm! Please note that this is a seasonal train and timetable can slighltly vary. Once you make the reservation for this tour you'll receive voucher for the train tickets so you will get the right information for timetable

data.name: Private Tour - Pisa & Lucca from Florence
data.description: Be enraptured by the magic cities of Pisa and Lucca during this private full-day tour by minivan from Florence. In just one day, this trip will allow you to discover two of the main cities of Tuscany. Stand under the famous Leaning Tower of Pisa and stroll around Piazza dei Miracoli accompanied by a licensed tourist guide. Be amazed by the elegant town of Lucca, a true paradise for all history and art lovers, famous for its medieval walls, and visit the nearby ancient forum.

data.name: Santa Croce Church Tour with Wine Tasting in Florence
data.description:

-Enjoy the company of a charismatic guide and knowledgeable cellar staff who will educate and amuse you with local wine-making facts and stories.

If you have a special love for all that is Italian, this is a perfect tour for you. Learn about Florentine history, explore Michelangelo's life, and visit the final resting places of Rossini, Machiavelli, Galileo Galilee, and more on this tour, including a visit to Santa Croce Church, the principal Franciscan church in Florence.
